entities.text: ATTENTION PARENTS: THESE TRANSGENDER TITLES ARE IN THE SCHOOL LIBRARY CATALOG Parents — this is a screenshot from a Follett Destiny school library catalog. These are listed as nonfiction / biography on the shelves, with interest levels that include young readers. You do not have to take my word for it. Open your district’s Destiny catalog, search the titles, and read the records yourself. Then decide whether this belongs on school shelves without your knowledge. Parents have a right to know what is being offered to their children. Share this with other parents who still think “it’s not in our schools.” Library portal link: https://fhsdschools.follettdestiny.com/portal/portal?app=Library%20Manager&appId=destiny-BHHB-JCJR&siteGuid=5F6A63B2-5BA7-4838-9AE9-C201E60B852E&nav=%252Fcataloging%252Fservlet%252Fhandlebasicsearchform.do IMPORTANT FOR PARENTS: If you do NOT want your child to have access to this type of content at school, you must contact your school's media specialist (librarian) or your child's principal. Written notification is required. Without it, your child will have full access to any book the school deems appropriate, even material such as this.

entities.author: School Watchlist
entities.text: URGENT: School Board Members Celebrating Calls for Violence Against a Parent This is the level of “public education” leadership we are dealing with in Francis Howell. A post from the page “No to Francis Howell Families for FHSD” openly celebrated the idea that an entire group of women “would happily yeet Lauren out of the nearest window.” Yeet = to throw something (or someone) with force. In plain English: they are joking about throwing a parent out a window. That is a call for violence. That is wishing harm on a mother. And what did the newly elected do? • Sara Dillard (current FHSD School Board member) gave it a heart. Sara Dillard - Director, Francis Howell Board of Education https://www.facebook.com/share/19UkKS1T9T/?mibextid=wwXIfr • Ren Boehms Adams (wife of newly elected board member Jason Adams and Theater Director at FH Middle) jumped in and claimed the post as “that’s me!!” Jason Adams for FHSD @Ren Boehms Adams https://www.facebook.com/share/14owBPCEkqH/?mibextid=wwXIfr • Jen Bahr (wife of re-elected St. Charles Director of Elections @kurt Bahr) and recently elected Cottleville Township committee woman, and associated with their Bahr family properties real estate @Jen Bahr https://www.facebook.com/share/1EiDTqGJ21/?mibextid=wwXIfr Citizens for Kurt Bahr Multiple others piled on with likes. To every single person who liked or loved that comment — including Sara Dillard, Ren Boehms Adams and Jen Bahr: Do you support throwing a parent out a window? Are you in favor of a parent’s death or serious harm? If the answer is no, then why didn’t you condemn it? Why did you celebrate it instead? This is not “online banter.” This is elected officials and their spouses normalizing violent rhetoric against a mother who simply advocated for her children and other parents in this district. Francis Howell School District and Board: this must be stopped and dealt with immediately. This is a call to Publicly remove these people from their leadership positions, condemn this behavior and the board members and family members who celebrated it. Silence is approval.

Meanwhile, there have been a number of times I've heard people who are supposedly in my own party angrily call for people to be tarred and feathered, which is clearly violent.

Don’t be afraid to speak out for your kids because they are voiceless and rely on you. Parents — Know Your Rights You do not have to accept every lesson, survey, or program the school offers. Here’s what you can do: Opt out of any content that does not align with your family’s values or beliefs. You have the right to review materials and formally opt your child out. Opt out of surveys and questionnaires. Many are designed to collect personal information about your child’s beliefs, mental health, family life, or identity. You can refuse participation. Request to preview all surveys, social-emotional lessons, and sensitive materials before they are given to your child. Put everything in writing. Send a clear opt-out notice and keep a copy for your records. Stay informed and connected. Talk with other parents, attend school board meetings, and share information. Your child’s education and values start at home. You have the right — and the responsibility — to protect both.

entities.text: FHSD Board Member Sara Dillard at Pride St. Charles (June 20, 2026) Sara Dillard, elected to the Francis Howell School District Board of Education in April 2026, shared this photo from the Pride St. Charles event. —>> SHE IS PICTURED WEARING HER OFFICIAL FRANCIS HOWELL SCHOOL DISTRICT NAME TAG WHILE ATTENDING <<— the event, which featured prominent rainbow and progress pride flags in the background. As a public school board member, this raises questions about personal advocacy and how it aligns with maintaining viewpoint neutrality in district policies, curriculum, and school environments that SERVE ALL FAMILIES. Wearing her official district name tag creates the appearance that FHSD endorses the event. District policies require viewpoint neutrality — personal views should not be presented as official school positions. This raises serious questions about policy violations and potential grounds for FORMAL REVIEW and DISMISSAL! What are your thoughts on elected officials participating in these events while representing the district? Original post from Sarah’s page: https://www.facebook.com/share/p/1ESFmPmzCD/?mibextid=wwXIfr

entities.text: Taxpayers, the Missouri State Auditor’s report on the Francis Howell School District’s superintendent hiring debacle with Dr. Mike Dominguez exposes wasted money and weak leadership. The district paid a search firm over $40,000 — yet we’ve never been refunded despite the $229k+ payout to a superintendent who never started. Some have said Board President Steven Blair was tasked with pursuing that refund. He allegedly heard “no,” tucked his tail, and backed down. Why does Steven Blair run to the lawyers for every move? Our legal expenses have more than doubled since FY 2022: • 2022: $96,627 • 2023: $107,880 • 2024: $134,130 • 2025: $216,980 • 2026: $144,116 YTD At this rate, 2026 could be our highest year yet — all on your tax dollars. Action step: Email Board President Steven Blair at steven.blair@fhsdschools.org and ask him why he didn’t fight harder for your tax dollars and why legal fees keep skyrocketing. Is this the passive leadership we want protecting our wallets? Real accountability means demanding better — not rolling over. Parents deserve board members who fight for fiscal responsibility. What do you think? #FHSD #TaxpayerAccountability #stevenblair #carolieowens #FHSD

entities.text: MORE TAX LEVIES COMING SOON? The full liberal FHSD school board says it’s never enough During the Prop RT fight, they warned of massive cuts (even threatening disability programs) if the tax freeze passed. Now that it failed — and they didn’t lose the $4M they claimed — they’re suddenly highlighting: • “No-Tax-Increase Debt Service Levy Transfer” • “No-Tax-Increase Bond Issue” So there are ways to shift money without a big tax hike? Why the scare tactics then (like threatening the Defunding the Disability program)? Taxpayers deserve straight answers, not selective urgency. The Result: Prevents Tax Relief You (and future homeowners) pay the current debt tax rate for many more years — often 10–20+ extra years. That adds up to thousands per homeowner over time. What do you think, FHSD families & St. Charles taxpayers? Stay tuned to board meetings. https://www.youtube.com/live/m_2hc5G4eCo?si=H5AOB8wP9h8rAUPP #FrancisHowell #PropRT #SchoolFunding

entities.text: TRANSPARENCY ISN’T HARASSMENT. PARENTAL INVOLVEMENT ISN’T EXTREMISM. If you classify bringing the TRUTH about what’s actually happening in your child’s classroom as “harassment,” then you’ve got a serious misconception about what harassment actually is. Sharing proof, of what’s being recommended or provided isn’t bullying — it’s called being an involved parent. It’s called transparency. It’s called PROTECTING KIDS and YOUR PARENTAL RIGHTS. Real harassment is trying to silence parents who dare to look inside the classroom and speak up about what they find. Real harassment is treating moms and dads like enemies for simply letting other parents know what their children are being taught and influenced. If we can’t agree on that basic principle, we’ve lost our way. What do you think — is speaking truth in your child’s education protected, or is it being twisted into something it’s not? Drop your thoughts below. #ParentalRights #EducationTransparency #KnowWhatsInTheClassroom #FHSD #FrancisHowell

entities.text: The Missouri NEA (teachers’ union) sued the state of Missouri. They tried to stop $50+ million in public tax money from going to the MOScholars program — a scholarship that helps certain kids (especially those with disabilities or from low-income families) pay for private school, homeschooling, tutoring, or therapy. The NEA argued the funding was done the wrong way (unconstitutional) and would hurt public schools. The judge dismissed the lawsuit completely. He ruled the NEA didn’t have the legal right to sue in this way, and even if they did, the funding was legal. The money can keep flowing to the scholarships.

entities.text: Wentzville School District Settles Transgender Bathroom Lawsuit with Missouri AG Great news for transparency and parental rights in Wentzville R-IV Schools! The district has reached a settlement with Attorney General Catherine Hanaway, resolving a 2023 Sunshine Law case. The board was accused of discussing a transgender student bathroom and locker room access policy in closed sessions (June 2023) instead of openly with the public. Key points of the April 2026 agreement: • No admission of wrongdoing by the district • Acknowledges parents’ fundamental right to know about and participate in decisions affecting their children’s education, safety, and welfare • Commits to full compliance with Missouri’s Open Meetings/Sunshine Law • Requires Sunshine Law training for board members and staff • Must post a public statement about the case and settlement on the district website This reinforces that important school policies should be debated in the open, not behind closed doors. Full settlement: https://ago.mo.gov/.../State-v.-Wentzville-Settlement... What do you think—transparency wins? Share your thoughts!

The board was accused of discussing a transgender student bathroom and locker room access policy in closed sessions (June 2023) instead of openly with the public. Key points of the April 2026 agreement: • No admission of wrongdoing by the district • Acknowledges parents’ fundamental right to know about and participate in decisions affecting their children’s education, safety, and welfare • Commits to full compliance with Missouri’s Open Meetings/Sunshine Law • Requires Sunshine Law training for board members and staff • Must post a public statement about the case and settlement on the district website This reinforces that important school policies should be debated in the open, not behind closed doors. Full settlement: https://ago.mo.gov/.../State-v.-Wentzville-Settlement... What do you think—transparency wins? Share your thoughts!

entities.text: Student Walk out UPDATE- Email from the district: let’s hope they follow their own rules February 12, 2026 FHN families: Some FHN students made the decision to leave their classes after 3rd period and walk out of the school building. FHN administrators are with the students and are directing students to move to a supervised location on campus. We are being told the walkout is a demonstration against recent actions by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). The District has provided guidance to all schools for navigating student protests. Our ultimate goal is to maintain a safe and secure school campus and to ensure that students do not present a major disruption to the learning environment. Here is some information about how we respond to student walkouts. We do not dismiss schools for walkouts, peaceful protests, or other demonstrations. Students who choose to participate in the walkout will be under adult supervision while on campus. Students will receive absence marks based on their actual attendance in each class, and they will face consequences for non-attendance or tardiness consistent with our normal procedures. Instruction will continue as scheduled. Students will not be given additional time to complete quizzes or exams that may be given during the walkout. Should a walkout happen during lunch, students who choose to participate will not be granted additional lunchtime. Consistent with MSHSAA bylaws and the FHSD Activities Handbook, students must attend school the entire day, or be marked excused by the principal, in order to participate in practices, rehearsals, or games for athletic teams or performance groups. Any verbal escalations, inappropriate behaviors, altercations, or other actions stemming from participation in the walkout will be subject to disciplinary action in accordance with the FHSD Code of Student Conduct. Students will be instructed to return to class as soon as the walkout concludes. Members of the media or general public wishing to observe or participate in the student-led walkout will not be permitted on campus during the instructional day. The principal has the authority to temporarily limit all traffic in and out, including parents and visitors, to protect student safety. Administrators and counselors will be available to assist students in processing their emotions. Every effort will be made to be consistent in our guidelines and consequences. The same policies and Code of Student Conduct that govern our work every day will also apply during any student walkouts. Thank you for helping us maintain safe learning environments for all students. FHN Admin Team

Students will receive absence marks based on their actual attendance in each class, and they will face consequences for non-attendance or tardiness consistent with our normal procedures. Instruction will continue as scheduled. Students will not be given additional time to complete quizzes or exams that may be given during the walkout. Should a walkout happen during lunch, students who choose to participate will not be granted additional lunchtime. Consistent with MSHSAA bylaws and the FHSD Activities Handbook, students must attend school the entire day, or be marked excused by the principal, in order to participate in practices, rehearsals, or games for athletic teams or performance groups. Any verbal escalations, inappropriate behaviors, altercations, or other actions stemming from participation in the walkout will be subject to disciplinary action in accordance with the FHSD Code of Student Conduct. Students will be instructed to return to class as soon as the walkout concludes. Members of the media or general public wishing to observe or participate in the student-led walkout will not be permitted on campus during the instructional day. The principal has the authority to temporarily limit all traffic in and out, including parents and visitors, to protect student safety. Administrators and counselors will be available to assist students in processing their emotions. Every effort will be made to be consistent in our guidelines and consequences. The same policies and Code of Student Conduct that govern our work every day will also apply during any student walkouts. Thank you for helping us maintain safe learning environments for all students. FHN Admin Team

entities.author: School Watchlist
entities.text: It’s CENSORSHIP. Voters should be paying attention. Instead of removing the inappropriate material, they’re now trying to rewrite policy to silence the only board member fighting for our kids innocence—effectively stripping a duly elected board member of her First Amendment rights. Let that sink in. Sexually explicit and wildly age-inappropriate books continue to be allowed in Francis Howell Schools (elementary included!). When school board member Jane Puszkar tries to shine a light on this—by reading the actual content aloud at board meetings and speaking out on conservative talk radio—the response from the mostly liberal board isn’t accountability. Rather than protect children or respect parents, the Francis Howell School Board is willing to go to unbelievable depths to cover their shame and suppress the truth. This isn’t about politics anymore. It’s about free speech, transparency, and protecting kids. Parents should be outraged. Voters should be paying attention.

entities.author: Nicole Ashraf
entities.text: Joy Hankey I can assure you that the standard of the test has not been lowered. In fact, in my 14 years of teaching, I have watched state assessments become increasingly rigorous and require students to demonstrate much deeper levels of thinking.And yes, our job is to teach children, but teaching and reaching children are not mutually exclusive. Students cannot effectively learn when they do not feel safe, supported, and connected at school. Maslow’s hierarchy of needs has long demonstrated that basic needs such as safety and belonging must be met before students are able to fully engage in learning.What has changed in recent years is that the district is finally providing teachers with resources that are much more closely aligned with Missouri state standards and evidence-based literacy practices, including the Science of Reading. When teachers have strong, standards-aligned curriculum and students feel safe enough to learn, that is when meaningful academic growth happens.Now that we have a decent reading resource, I’m hopeful that we can get an aligned math resource. We haven’t had math resources aligned with our state standards since 2011 (at least in elementary). Reaching children is part of teaching them.

entities.author: Rhianna Gonzales
entities.text: Honestly I’d rather it be this way. Not because I personally want my kids to be device dependent but that’s how the world is heading and been heading. To keep them up with the current times of learning to navigate devices is a “crucial” step into stepping into a digital world. If it was my way we’d be doing books and handwriting. The legit concerns are there but this is how we prep our kids for the future. Whether we agree with it or not on that’s how our future should be-it is what it is. I think they also have safety measures and parental controls on it in a sense, where they can’t access certain websites and can’t just put anything on the tablets, I think the district already has blocked sites and apps. So the kids can’t just hop on there and play Roblox or anything crazy like that.

entities.author: Shannon Senzig
entities.text: Julie Layton They don't have to be "big books like back in the day," though. That's a false dichotomy. Those books were designed with longevity in mind. They were expected to last for 15 years, so they were hardbound and huge. As a result, lots of schools had to make due with damaged, old, and out of date books that the students had to copy from. What we need are smaller, paperback, single use work books for each student. These have always been around, but the hardbound mega-books were thought to be cheaper so most school districts went that route, with maybe the exception being spelling. Remembering hand copying all those math problems and grammar lessons into a notebook? And pages and pages of wasted space full of illustrations and fluff to justify making the book as expensive as possible? That was completely unnecessary and not what was best for kids. Meanwhile, subjects that do require a text such as science and social studies can be done online in the classroom and study guides can be sent home instead.

entities.author: John Smith
entities.text: Marianna Pagis My statement was a general one, as proof, that is why the U.S. Postal System is struggling because their income from mail has decreased by 30-40% each year over the last 10 years. As far as the "glitches" go, that tends to be internet access and battery life. Textbooks on Chromebooks offer a lot more than your standard textbook. They can be updated instantly, errors in print can be fixed without having to order new books, the cost is a fraction of a hard copy and they offer interactive tools like search's, zoom, read-aloud and teacher added highlights and links.

entities.author: School Watchlist
entities.text: Ashley Goodwin Equal access matters, but a school-issued Chromebook isn’t the only (or safest) way to provide it. Proving to only families in need would be cost efficient and logical. Monitoring school Wi-Fi doesn’t cover off-network use, personal accounts, or apps students add themselves. A family smartphone is parent-controlled; a district device is not.Most classes no longer issue a full set of physical textbooks, so the backpack-weight comparison doesn’t hold. The real differences are distraction, screen time, content students can reach, and how much visibility parents actually have.

entities.text: Ashley Goodwin it’s obvious you don’t work in a school. I have seen these kids bypass the school security all the time. NOTHING HAPPENS. I heard a stat that 99% of the people have smartphones, which means they have WiFi access in some way. But I advocate getting rid of 1:1 tech for all kids-bring back pen and paper. Most of my kids’ teachers did and have found retention of material has improved tremendously. They only use Chromebooks for tests, which does not require a 1:1 scenario.

entities.author: Shannon Senzig
entities.text: Ashley Goodwin I don't want my kid to have "equal access" though. I don't want my kid to have any access to porn, to social media, to websites trying to steal their identity, to AI generated psychology. I don't want them playing video games at school. I want them reading well-curated literature and quality texts. I want them learning to write, spell, and do math with their hands as EVERY study ever done shows that this is the best method for brain development and retention of skills. What good is "equal access" if what is being accessed is garbage? Ideally, all kids would be exposed to a high quality education, but absent that option, I'm fine with my kid have different access than other kids.

entities.author: School Watchlist
entities.text: THIS 1:1 TECH POLICY SHOULDN’T BE HAPPENING TO OUR KIDS Francis Howell middle and high school students are required to take home district Chromebooks starting August 26 for FHN and carry them every single day. Extra weight in already heavy backpacks + more mandatory screen time is a direct hit on kids’ bodies and minds. Physical: Research consistently shows backpacks exceeding 10-15% of a student’s body weight increase neck, shoulder, and back pain plus postural problems. https://www.healthychildren.org/.../Backpack-Safety.aspx Emotional: Higher screen time is linked to increased anxiety and depression symptoms in adolescents. https://www.frontiersin.org/.../fpubh.2023.1101594/full Parents — push back. Email the Board of Education at board@fhsdschools.org and ask them to reconsider mandatory daily Chromebook carry and the added physical + emotional burden this places on students.

entities.text: Parkway tried this on our family. We told them no. No chromebooks in our house. I told my daughter's principal that if I found a Chromebook in her backpack one more time, I would confiscate it and lock it up and it would be HIS responsibility to come see me during my mommy office hours and pick it up in person. They stopped sending it home. Other parents did the same. The elementary teachers have stopped sending them home and only offer it as an option for the summer.

entities.author: Sarah Hurst
entities.text: The school has indicated that this policy will not increase screen time. Policies remain the same in this regard. However, I do have some concern about how heavy the backpacks will be for my new 6th grader. She does plan to use her locker but is worried about getting to class on time. It will definitely increase the weight of the bags. I have heard that there may be a way for students to charge their devices at school daily for parents not wishing their student to bring them home if necessary. I figure why get all upset when we don't even know how this will all shake down? If it becomes a problem, THEN deal with it. No need to fix things that aren't a current problem Do not worry about tomorrow for today has enough trouble of its own! (Matthew 6:34)

entities.text: THIS 1:1 TECH POLICY SHOULDN’T BE HAPPENING TO OUR KIDS Francis Howell middle and high school students are required to take home district Chromebooks starting August 26 for FHN and carry them every single day. Extra weight in already heavy backpacks + more mandatory screen time is a direct hit on kids’ bodies and minds. Physical: Research consistently shows backpacks exceeding 10-15% of a student’s body weight increase neck, shoulder, and back pain plus postural problems. https://www.healthychildren.org/.../Backpack-Safety.aspx Emotional: Higher screen time is linked to increased anxiety and depression symptoms in adolescents. https://www.frontiersin.org/.../fpubh.2023.1101594/full Parents — push back. Email the Board of Education at board@fhsdschools.org and ask them to reconsider mandatory daily Chromebook carry and the added physical + emotional burden this places on students.

entities.text: MISSION CREEP “Neurodiverse Learner” – This language is not neutral. It comes from a progressive educational framework that often treats neurological differences primarily through an identity/acceptance lens rather than a clinical or developmental one. Many of these approaches emphasize co-regulation and validation in ways that can undermine clear parental leadership. Parents - you should want to know exactly which organizations will be present. In many districts these fairs become soft entry points for progressive mental health groups, identity-affirming organizations, or curriculum-linked nonprofits.

versions.text: Student Walk out UPDATE- Email from the district: let’s hope they follow their own rules February 12, 2026 FHN families: Some FHN students made the decision to leave their classes after 3rd period and walk out of the school building. FHN administrators are with the students and are directing students to move to a supervised location on campus. We are being told the walkout is a demonstration against recent actions by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). The District has provided guidance to all schools for navigating student protests. Our ultimate goal is to maintain a safe and secure school campus and to ensure that students do not present a major disruption to the learning environment. Here is some information about how we respond to student walkouts. We do not dismiss schools for walkouts, peaceful protests, or other demonstrations. Students who choose to participate in the walkout will be under adult supervision while on campus. Students will receive absence marks based on their actual attendance in each class, and they will face consequences for non-attendance or tardiness consistent with our normal procedures. Instruction will continue as scheduled. Students will not be given additional time to complete quizzes or exams that may be given during the walkout. Should a walkout happen during lunch, students who choose to participate will not be granted additional lunchtime. Consistent with MSHSAA bylaws and the FHSD Activities Handbook, students must attend school the entire day, or be marked excused by the principal, in order to participate in practices, rehearsals, or games for athletic teams or performance groups. Any verbal escalations, inappropriate behaviors, altercations, or other actions stemming from participation in the walkout will be subject to disciplinary action in accordance with the FHSD Code of Student Conduct. Students will be instructed to return to class as soon as the walkout concludes. Members of the media or general public wishing to observe or participate in the student-led walkout will not be permitted on campus during the instructional day. The principal has the authority to temporarily limit all traffic in and out, including parents and visitors, to protect student safety. Administrators and counselors will be available to assist students in processing their emotions. Every effort will be made to be consistent in our guidelines and consequences. The same policies and Code of Student Conduct that govern our work every day will also apply during any student walkouts. Thank you for helping us maintain safe learning environments for all students. FHN Admin Team

entities.author: School Watchlist
entities.text: PARENTS THE LONGER YOU WAIT and you don't hold your child's schools accountable gives these guys more time to dictate what's best for your child's physical mental and emotional health. Don’t be afraid to speak out for your kids because they are voiceless and rely on you. Parents — Know Your Rights You do not have to accept every lesson, survey, or program the school offers. Here’s what you can do: Opt out of any content that does not align with your family’s values or beliefs. You have the right to review materials and formally opt your child out. Opt out of surveys and questionnaires. Many are designed to collect personal information about your child’s beliefs, mental health, family life, or identity. You can refuse participation. Request to preview all surveys, social-emotional lessons, and sensitive materials before they are given to your child. Put everything in writing. Send a clear opt-out notice and keep a copy for your records. Stay informed and connected. Talk with other parents, attend school board meetings, and share information. Your child’s education and values start at home. You have the right — and the responsibility — to protect both.

entities.text: CARL DROPS THE MATH HAMMER ON PROP H Schooling the District on “Free Money” VOTE NO on Prop H The ballot will say $150 million. That’s only the face value of the bonds — not the real cost to taxpayers. We’ve seen this before. Prop S in 2020 said $244 million. The final price tag? $294 million. That’s $50 MILLION MORE than voters approved! How did they do it? They intentionally set higher-than-market interest rates so investors would pay a “premium.” The district got extra cash upfront. Taxpayers get stuck with higher interest payments for the next 10–20 years. The district will try to call that extra $50 million “free money.” There is no such thing as free money. It’s basic time value of money. The mathematics hasn’t changed. They can pick whatever number they want — they just need to be transparent about the true total cost. So far, they’re still refusing to do that. Until the district tells taxpayers the real maximum amount they’ll actually spend, Vote No on Prop H. Share this so more people know what’s really at stake. Listen to common sense Carl >>> https://www.youtube.com/live/gXJwYo-H72c...

entities.text: 1:1 TECHNOLOGY IS COMING TO ALL FHSD MIDDLE & HIGH SCHOOLS Every middle and high school student gets their own take-home Chromebook this fall. Elementary stays with classroom carts. IF IT SOUNDS TOO GOOD TO BE TRUE… IT IS. DO THEY REALLY THINK WE’RE THAT STUPID? The district says this will “save $300,000 a year.” Reality check: • Damage & loss rates jump when devices go home every day (8–12% annually) • Hardware is only ~25% of the real cost — repairs, IT support, and replacements eat the rest • Other districts have spent tens of millions fixing broken Chromebooks that only last 2–3 years • Parents still get hit with repair/replacement fees They also claim “no more screen time.” Giving every middle & high schooler a personal device makes that hard to believe. More screens. Higher long-term costs. This is not a win for students or taxpayers. CONTACT: board@fhsdschools.org

versions.text: 1:1 TECHNOLOGY IS COMING TO ALL FHSD MIDDLE & HIGH SCHOOLS Every middle and high school student gets their own take-home Chromebook this fall. Elementary stays with classroom carts. IF IT SOUNDS TOO GOOD TO BE TRUE… IT IS. DO THEY REALLY THINK WE’RE THAT STUPID? The district says this will “save $300,000 a year.” Reality check: • Damage & loss rates jump when devices go home every day (8–12% annually) • Hardware is only ~25% of the real cost — repairs, IT support, and replacements eat the rest • Other districts have spent tens of millions fixing broken Chromebooks that only last 2–3 years • Parents still get hit with repair/replacement fees They also claim “no more screen time.” Giving every middle & high schooler a personal device makes that hard to believe. More screens. Higher long-term costs. This is not a win for students or taxpayers. CONTACT: board@fhsdschools.org

entities.text: BOOK ALERT The book: Amazons, Abolitionists, and Activists: A Graphic History of Women’s Fight for Their Rights by Mikki Kendall Library: Francis Howell Central Is marketed as a history of women’s rights. In reality, it is a progressive, intersectional feminist narrative that reframes the entire story through modern identity politics. It uses a classroom framing device to walk readers through history while pushing a clear ideological agenda. This book contains: • Explicit inclusion of LGBTQ rights and gender ideology as core parts of “women’s rights” • Promotion of reproductive rights / abortion as a central women’s issue • Intersectional framing that elevates race and identity politics above classical equality or biblical views of men and women • Criticism of early women’s suffrage leaders (including white feminists) for not being progressive enough on race and other modern causes • A strong call to ongoing leftist-style activism presented as the natural continuation of the fight for rights • Adult political content delivered in an accessible graphic novel format aimed at teens If your child is in Francis Howell Central and checking out graphic histories, this is one worth previewing yourself. Not every book with “women’s rights” in the title is teaching the same values. IMPORTANT FOR PARENTS: If you do NOT want your child to have access to this type of content at school, you must contact your school's media specialist (librarian) or your child's principal. Written notification is required. Without it, your child will have full access to any book the school deems appropriate, even material such as this. You can also: • Request a list of books your child has already checked out. • Sign up to receive daily email notifications of every book your child checks out. These options are available at both the elementary and secondary levels. I've said this before, and I'll say it again: we no longer live in an age where adults are protecting children from sexual content. We are living in an age where adults are offering minor children books with age-inappropriate sexual content under the guise of education. I will never stop fighting for our children because every single one of them are worth fighting for! entities.text: JD Kunkler I agree full medical transitions are rare. And inattentive parents are usually the ones with vulnerable children. However, it still doesn’t make it right. There is a real institutional push to create secrecy and treat parental opposition as harm.The main route is social transition first. Schools and counselors change the child’s name, pronouns, and facilities under “affirmation” policies — often without telling parents. This isn’t theoretical. It’s documented policy in multiple states and districts, and parents have sued over it.Medical steps (blockers, hormones) are harder to hide, but pathways still exist: clinics that prioritize the minor’s identity and delay parents, one parent acting against the other, or activist networks steering kids around parental consent.Minors don’t pay for this themselves. The money comes from Medicaid or insurance in some states, activist grants, crowdfunding, or one parent funding it in secret.Calling concern over this a “dog whistle” is not accurate. This is a warning.

entities.text: PARENTS OF FHSD — WE NEED YOUR EYES AND EARS ON THE GROUND ( & in your student’s hands. Ie check the parental settings on their cell phones) you see anything concerning in our schools ( or your child’s cell phone, tablet or chrome book) — whether it’s materials ( internet, instagram, Snapchat) practices ( tic toc videos ) or influences that undermine parental rights ( social media influencers or your child’s social networks) and our children’s innocence ( tic toc videos YouTube or other streaming services ) — please reach out or look in a mirror. You can remain completely anonymous or clueless if you wish. Your observations help us shine the light and stand together for what’s best for our kids.Remember: We have every right to know what’s happening in our schools and to hold them ( Parents & STUDENTS ) accountable.Some adjustments were made to your original comment to try and clarify where the confusion is coming from. Teachers are trying their best to educate your children and cannot compete with these outside influences or while under attack from certain people.

entities.text: Jane Puszkar Thank you for the laugh—I genuinely laughed out loud.As a believer, I can't help but think of the Gospels. They repeatedly portray Jesus spending time with people who were marginalized, criticized, rejected, publicly shamed, and considered the "wrong" people by the religious leaders of His day. In fact, He was often criticized for doing exactly that.I know you were trying to make a point, but I think you may have made the opposite one.If you go back and reread this thread, what I'm advocating for is conversation. I'm encouraging people to sit with others, build relationships, partner together, and understand one another.What you're describing is public shaming and throwing stones.To me, that's exactly why I made my original comment. I believe conversation changes hearts far more often than condemnation ever does.

entities.text: Karin Fitzgerald Robinette you’re trying to distort God’s Word to fit your mold—so you can call what God calls sin something it is not, in hopes of being accepted into His holy Kingdom. This is a grave error.God creates us male and female in His image (Genesis 1:27; 5:2). Psalm 139 celebrates His design in the womb—not our feelings redefining it. Leviticus 18:22 declares, “You shall not lie with a male as with a woman; it is an abomination.” Romans 1:27 warns that men “burned in their lust for one another… receiving in themselves the penalty of their error which was due.”True love (1 John 4:7) “rejoices with the truth” (1 Cor 13:6) and calls sinners to repentance, not celebration of sin (Romans 1:24-27; 1 Cor 6:9-11).David and Jonathan’s friendship was deep and honorable, not sexual. Galatians 3:28 means equal value in salvation, not erasing God’s created order (Matt 19:4-6).Real love points people to Christ and holiness. I pray we both stand on the whole counsel of God.

entities.text: Livica Holliday - to be fair it wasn’t Fifty Shades of Grey but at the same time it’s not appropriate option for seventh graders at school. Personally, I let my children read and watch a lot of content many parents wouldn’t approve of. But that was my choice and it was under my terms and I developed wonderful teenagers with wonderful morals and astounding grades. ￼I do wanna talk￼ about Pride a little bit, though. ￼This teacher is obviously enthusiastic about pride to a degree where it has become a disruption. I don’t think parents are trying to pretend like gay people don’t exist. I think they want to explain what being gay is to their children in their own terms. Parent are entitled that- especially at such a vulnerable age. ￼

entities.text: Matt Stolle I absolutely want to improve schools, I want improved educational results, I want family partnerships (as a parent and as an educator). I have never seen improvement from bullying, from publicly shaming people, from making enemies of someone who I deeply wish a partnership with. I believe that those partnerships happen from listening to experiences, honoring parent beliefs, respecting best educational practices, and meeting each child where they are. Do you believe partnerships are grown when we publicly shame each other? When instead of a conversations to understand, we publicly call each other out.

Your job is to teach core subjects — not to promote or encourage any particular lifestyle, sexual identity, or ideology to other people’s children. Stay in your lane as an educator, respect parental rights, and don’t exhaust yourself. *** This teacher was found to maintain an in-classroom PRIDE library at Hollenbeck. Parents deserve transparency: Will those same books and ideology follow them to their new position at Bryan Middle School? *** PARENTS HAVE THE RIGHT TO KNOW. Email: ryan.johnson@fhsdschools.org Bryan Middle Principal

entities.text: PARENTS OF FHSD — WE NEED YOUR EYES AND EARS ON THE GROUND! you see anything concerning in our schools — whether it’s curriculum, materials, practices, or influences that seem to undermine parental rights and our children’s innocence — please reach out. entities.text: SCHOOL FUNDING REALITY CHECK: STOP THE ENDLESS MONEY REQUESTS - THE DATA DOESN’T LIE — WHY IS IT NEVER ENOUGH? Hey School Board — what’s your story this time? Blaming the state doesn’t work when the data shows revenue is UP $7.1M this year and $17M over five years. Try again. At last night’s FHSD Board meeting, Carl Suri (the man in the orange shirt) delivered one of the clearest, most data-driven explanations I’ve heard about school funding. He didn’t get emotional. He just walked through the actual numbers: • District revenue is now $245 million — up $7.1 million this year alone • That increase came entirely from the state (up 10.75%) • Over the last five years, state revenue is up $17 million — a 32% increase • Per-student state funding is at an all-time high, even after inflation His point was simple and hard to argue with: the money keeps going up, yet the district still acts like it’s never enough. He questioned why we keep hearing calls for more local taxes or fund transfers when the data shows revenue has been rising steadily. If you’ve ever felt like “just a little more money” is a permanent answer instead of a temporary one, watch this segment. It’s calm, factual, and cuts through the usual talking points. Link starts right at his comments: https://www.youtube.com/live/SwzYuBTzlnQ?t=218 Watch it. Share it. The numbers matter.

entities.text: TEACHER CLAIMS VICTIMHOOD AFTER YEARS OF PUBLIC TRANSGENDER ADVOCACY — BUT WHAT ABOUT THE KIDS? Independence Elementary Kindergarten Teacher Becky Hormuth (~20:24) spoke as a victim of supposed bullying and defamation, asking the board for more staff protections. Questions that need answers: • Why is it that when the truth is shared about policies affecting children, staff get to become the victim — while innocent children (including kindergarteners!) are expected to quietly accept changes to bathrooms, social transitions, or gender ideology without their parents’ full knowledge and consent? • Is it not true your own child has transitioned? • Was there not news media coverage in which you voluntarily participated? • Did you not stand up at multiple public school board meetings advocating against sex-based policies for district facilities? • Was the child who came home asking why they’d want to be a boy not connected to your classroom? Parents aren’t harassers for asking hard questions and protecting their kids. The double standard is clear: data and parental rights matter. Watch the full meeting and decide for yourselves. Link (Hormuth segment starts here): https://www.youtube.com/live/SwzYuBTzlnQ?t=1224 What do you think, FHSD families?

entities.author: School Watchlist
entities.text: The U.S. Department of Justice and the U.S. Department of Education announced they will pursue enforcement action against Kansas City, Kansas Public Schools, alleging the district violated federal parental-rights and student-privacy laws by shielding students' transgender status from parents. Federal investigators pointed to a district policy stating that school staff "should not disclose information that may reveal a student's transgender status or gender nonconforming presentation to others, including parents." The Education Department's Student Privacy Policy Office opened its investigation in August 2025; in April 2026, it found the district's policy violated the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act, and in June it issued a formal Letter of Impending Enforcement Action after also finding a Title IX violation. Read more in the comments....

entities.text: FERPA Opt-Out Reminder for FHSD Families Did you know? FERPA allows schools to share certain "directory information" (such as a student's name, grade level, honors, activities, or photos) unless a parent/guardian chooses to opt out. You may want to opt out if you prefer that your student's information and/or photos not be included in school publications, websites, social media, yearbooks, news releases, or other approved communications. FHSD Public Notices & FERPA Opt-Out Information: https://www.fhsdschools.org/public-notices Opt Out Form: https://resources.finalsite.net/.../FERPA-and-Media-Opt... Please review the information carefully to determine what is best for your family.

entities.text: JD Kunkler Jesus ate with sinners to call them to repentance, not to affirm their sin (Mark 2:17). Loving my neighbor includes speaking truth in love - believe it or not I do care about these people. I pray for them nightly, but I believe what they’re doing is evil and needs to be called out. It’s hard to sound “loving” on FB, especially when protecting children from age-inappropriate ideology in public schools.The School Watchlist isn’t exclusion—it’s transparency for all parents. Schools should stay neutral on contested sexual/gender issues instead of pushing one side with flags, curricula, and events. That doesn’t stop anyone from practicing their faith; it prevents schools from undermining mine and parental rights.I don’t have a planks in my eye about this —that scripture means “don’t be a hypocrite”. And parental stewardship isn’t ‘superiority’; it’s obedience (Proverbs 22:6, Ephesians 6:4). We can love people while refusing to let public institutions confuse kids on biology and God’s design.

entities.author: Kaylee Morris
entities.text: Jane Puszkar I never screamed or mentioned the separation of church and state. I simply asked School Watchlist a question, but since you brought that up yourself, I’ll inform you more accurately.First, your claim that “the country was founded on Christian values” is not supported by historical records. The Founders came from diverse Christian denominations, but they explicitly rejected the idea of a government tied to any religion. After independence, there was widespread agreement that the new nation must not have an official religion, and that government must not endorse or support any church.Source: https://www.loc.gov/exhibits/religion/rel06.htmlSecond, the idea that “separation of church and state was meant to keep government out of religion, not religion out of government” is also incorrect. Thomas Jefferson, the very person who coined the phrase, stated clearly in his 1802 letter to the Danbury Baptists that the First Amendment builds “a wall of separation between Church and State.” That wall protects both directions, government cannot interfere with religion, and religion cannot wield government power or receive government endorsement.Source: https://founders.archives.gov/documents/Jefferson/01-36-02-0056Roger Williams, founder of Rhode Island, also argued that government involvement corrupts religion and that a “hedge or wall of separation” is necessary to keep the church pure and independent.Source: https://americanheritage.org/roger-williams-first-call-for-separation-of-church-and-state-in-america/Third, your suggestion that religion was intended to be part of government contradicts the Constitution itself. Article VI explicitly prohibits any religious test for public office, ensuring that government positions are open to people of all faiths or none. This was a deliberate rejection of the idea that the United States government should be Christian or tied to Christianity.Source: https://constitution.congress.gov/constitution/article-6/Finally, the Establishment Clause, mostly written by James Madison, was created because the Founders had seen firsthand the harm caused when governments endorse or enforce religion. They agreed that the federal government must stay neutral toward religion, and by 1833 every state had disestablished its official church.Source: https://constitutioncenter.org/the-constitution/amendments/amendment-i/interpretations/264So no, the Founders did not intend religion to guide government, nor did they believe the United States was founded on Christian values in any governmental sense. They intentionally built a system where religion is personal, not governmental, and where public officials must not use their government roles to promote their personal faith.If you are going to talk about the separation of church and state, you should at least talk about it accurately. These are literal words straight from our Founders and the Constitution. Please educate yourself

entities.text: Margarita Jasmine a regular church service is a worship gathering. The core purpose is religious practice (prayer, sacraments, sermon, and communal worship). It's for the congregation, oriented toward God/the divine, even if visitors are welcome.A community event held at a church (a food drive, a concert, a blood donation clinic, a public forum) uses the church as a venue, but the activity itself isn't a religious rite. The building is just the location; the purpose is secular or civic, even if there's a Christian motivation behind hosting it.I hope that helps.

entities.author: Bryan Medlin
entities.text: The Francis Howell School District has an obligation to treat all students and staff with equal dignity and respect — and that includes LGBTQ+ students and educators who are part of this community every single day. The selective removal or suppression of content that represents certain groups, while allowing others, is not neutral — it is a policy choice, and it sends a message.One has to wonder: if this were a religious or faith-based activity, would it have even been questioned? The inconsistency in how content is treated depending on the group involved is impossible to ignore, and it raises serious concerns about whether this district is applying its standards fairly and equitably across the board.I want to recognize Board of Education member Sara Dillard, who has shown the kind of principled, inclusive leadership this district desperately needs. Her attendance at the St. Charles Gay Pride event is a powerful example of what it looks like when an elected official truly shows up for all members of their community — not just the ones it’s comfortable or convenient to support. This is the standard we should expect from every elected official, every teacher, and every principal in this district. Representation and visibility from those in positions of authority matters deeply to students who are watching and looking for someone to stand in their corner.To the rest of the district’s leadership: I am a Francis Howell graduate, and I expect better. Every child in this district — regardless of who they are or who they love — deserves to feel that their school stands with them. I urge you to examine your decisions carefully and ask whether they would hold up to a standard of true equity. The community is watching !!!

entities.author: Jonah E Tate
entities.text: School Watchlist I disagree. I think educators have to tailor themselves to each student, because each student comes from very different homes and backgrounds. When taking ed courses at Truman, this was addressed and taught. Every decision, from the curriculum to the setup of the classroom, reflects a set of values. Seeing and experiencing other beliefs around you isn’t indoctrination; it’s a part of life. By separating ourselves from one another, and labeling people different than ourselves as “others” or an outsiders we aren’t protecting these kids from having “beliefs forced on them”, we’re helping them see it as something different or wrong. it’s not the compassion jesus taught. Seeing how diverse our country and state is, is part of the beauty of the US. Embrace diversity, and it won’t feel so different. As educators we should embrace every child’s differences, and tailor our classroom and teaching styles to their needs. Whether that’s a need for a more hands-on learning with projects, a need for lunch assistance for a child, or a child feeling confused about their identity and needing a safe space. We should always give that to them because in the end, we are there for them.

entities.author: Katherine Amanda
entities.text: School Watchlist can you please explain to me what related to the faith of Christian families is being sidelined? Is your expectation that all school policies align with your Christian beliefs and values? Can you explain to me how asking others to elevate your belief system (ideological view) is ok, but asking you to respect the gender/sexuality of others is not? I also want to understand why you think someone else being gay, queer or trans or whatever impacts or affects you. Do you believe that children become LGBTQ by watching others be LGBTQ? If this is true, how come kids who grow up in Christian families, watching Christian marriages, grow up to be LGBTQ? And finally, if you believe in God and predestination - why do you have to convince anyone else about Gods goodness, or interfere with another persons journey to God as a stumbling block (Jesus taught change in behavior through acceptance and love) wouldn’t that mean all of our paths are already decided? I’m not looking for a fight. I’m honestly and earnestly trying to understand your perspective and how it fits in with your belief system (there are many denominations and pathways to Christ, but I’m assuming you are somewhere within the non denominational/baptist sect). I also must add that I have a very deeply involved and educated history related to Christian religion. If you choose to respond with defensiveness or as if I need to be taught something instead of giving an honest and considered response, you’ll just be ignored. I also get it if you choose to ignore my questions.

entities.author: Wayne Patrick
entities.text: I looked into the board conduct issue, and the claim here seems overstated. FHSD does have board-conduct and ethics policies, but the available policy language is about board members acting professionally, not acting individually on behalf of the Board, and understanding that authority rests with the Board as a body in a legal session. I have not seen a policy that says wearing a board name tag at a public community event automatically equals district endorsement.At most, someone could ask whether the name tag created confusion about whether she was there personally or officially. That is a fair question. But jumping from that to “formal review and dismissal” is a huge leap unless someone can cite the exact FHSD policy and the exact legal removal process. An elected board member attending a public, family-friendly community event is not the same thing as the district formally endorsing that event.

entities.text: https://www.nea.org/resource-library/educator-rights-and-political-participationEducators have strong First Amendment rights to engage in political activity on your own time and in your personal capacity.You should make it clear that you are not speaking for your employer or acting on its behalf.This is an ethics violation, regardless of individuals support for her actions. Would the same people support an employee wearing a school name badge to a Trump rally or to church? Just because you personally don't agree with it. A formal complain should be made if this really did happen.​"Local Policy & Ethics Violations​Most school districts have strict board policies regarding political activity. These policies typically explicitly forbid board members or staff from using district equipment, logos, or insignia (like badges) for partisan political purposes. If a complaint is filed, the board member could face internal censure, reprimand, or an ethics investigation."

entities.text: FHSD Board Member Sara Dillard at Pride St. Charles (June 20, 2026) Sara Dillard, elected to the Francis Howell School District Board of Education in April 2026, shared this photo from the Pride St. Charles event. —>> SHE IS PICTURED WEARING HER OFFICIAL FRANCIS HOWELL SCHOOL DISTRICT NAME TAG WHILE ATTENDING <<— the event, which featured prominent rainbow and progress pride flags in the background. As a public school board member, this raises questions about personal advocacy and how it aligns with maintaining viewpoint neutrality in district policies, curriculum, and school environments that SERVE ALL FAMILIES. Wearing her official district name tag creates the appearance that FHSD endorses the event. District policies require viewpoint neutrality — personal views should not be presented as official school positions. This raises serious questions about policy violations and potential grounds for FORMAL REVIEW and DISMISSAL! What are your thoughts on elected officials participating in these events while representing the district? entities.text: True love doesn’t require us to celebrate what God calls sin. The world says, “Affirm me or you’re hateful.” But Scripture says otherwise.“Woe to those who call evil good and good evil…” (Isaiah 5:20)And “Have nothing to do with the fruitless deeds of darkness, but rather EXPOSE THEM.” (Ephesians 5:11)We can love people without lying to them. Parents, stand firm. Churches, speak truth. Live and let live is one thing—forced celebration of sin is another.God’s Word is our standard, not cultural pressure. Pray for those in deception, but do not bow.#BiblicalTruth #StandFirm #LoveDoesNotAffirmSin

entities.text: I don’t believe that Kehoe is going to sign SB1002. However if he doesn’t veto it , then SB 1002 will become law. If he vetoes it then that means their request for MORE money will be placed on Next April‘s ballot. The good news about not signing is that Steven Blair and Carolie Owens do not get an extra 18 months in office and they will both go through an election process next April. I hope everyone is paying attention. They will be asking to be voted back in and at the same time, have their hands in your pocket for more money. Nobody in their right mind would vote them back in especially after the superintendent debacle. Stay tuned Saint Charles. We’ve got a county to save.

entities.text: FHSD Parents & Taxpayers: Questions on the New “No Tax Rate Increase” Props O & H Headed to November The Board just voted to put two propositions on the November 3, 2026 ballot that they’re marketing as “no-tax-rate-increase” measures. Here’s the quick breakdown: Proposition O – Levy Transfer Shifts 12.5 cents from the debt service levy to the operating levy. The district says this will add roughly $5.5 million per year to the operating budget (for salaries, buses, food service, etc.) without raising your overall tax rate. They cite a ~$9.3 million state funding shortfall over the next two years plus rising costs for labor, insurance, fuel, and supplies. Proposition H – $150 Million Bond Issue For “critical facility needs” across all 23 schools — roofs, windows, HVAC, mechanical/electrical systems, safety & security, CTE programs, ADA compliance, sidewalks, parking lots, and athletic/performing arts spaces. Also pitched as no tax rate increase. I have some real questions about these: • For Prop O: Is there really a $9M+ state funding shortfall hitting us this hard right now? What’s the actual story behind the funding formula changes? We need the full, transparent picture — not just the headline number. • For Prop H: It’s interesting they don’t say what will happen to our current bond levy rate if this does NOT pass. Would it actually go down once existing obligations are paid off? And did they have to do any maneuvering or creative structuring to get this labeled a true “no tax increase” bond issue? This comes right after our Prop S experience. What started as a $240 million bond ended up adding another $150 million in costs (totaling around $390 million) because it wasn’t planned or executed right the first time. We can’t keep repeating that pattern. Transparency on these big fiscal moves matters. Our kids, our teachers, and our community deserve straight answers and better planning before we head to the polls. See the attached PDF from the recent board meeting update for the details they released. https://go.boarddocs.com/mo/fhsdmo/Board.nsf/Public# https://www.fhsdschools.org/.../distric.../post/prop-o-and-h What do you think? Do these questions matter to you too? Have you looked at the numbers? Drop your thoughts in the comments — and keep pushing for real accountability. Share this if you believe more FHSD families should see it. #FHSD #FrancisHowell #PropO #PropH #SchoolBond #TaxTransparency #StCharlesCounty

entities.text: STOP THE FAILING SCREEN TIME TREND IN FHSD! • Schools nationwide are ditching excessive screens and returning to pen and paper — and students are thriving • Middle schoolers spent ~70 minutes daily on screens last year; districts limiting devices are seeing real gains • One AP Literature teacher banned phones and laptops: reading confidence soared from 46% to 95%, and students went from struggling to write half a page to producing 6-7 pages by hand • Teachers are reporting major improvements in attention span, focus, motor skills, and engagement Parents: Demand our Francis Howell School District rejects this failing screen-heavy trend. entities.text: Taxpayers, the Missouri State Auditor’s report on the Francis Howell School District’s superintendent hiring debacle with Dr. Mike Dominguez exposes wasted money and weak leadership. The district paid a search firm over $40,000 — yet we’ve never been refunded despite the $229k+ payout to a superintendent who never started. Some have said Board President Steven Blair was tasked with pursuing that refund. He allegedly heard “no,” tucked his tail, and backed down. Why does Steven Blair run to the lawyers for every move? Our legal expenses have more than doubled since FY 2022: • 2022: $96,627 • 2023: $107,880 • 2024: $134,130 • 2025: $216,980 • 2026: $144,116 YTD At this rate, 2026 could be our highest year yet — all on your tax dollars. Action step: Email Board President Steven Blair at steven.blair@fhsdschools.org and ask him why he didn’t fight harder for your tax dollars and why legal fees keep skyrocketing. Is this the passive leadership we want protecting our wallets? Real accountability means demanding better — not rolling over. Parents deserve board members who fight for fiscal responsibility. What do you think? #FHSD #TaxpayerAccountability #stevenblair #carolieowens #FHSD

It still needs to pass the Senate and be signed by the President to become law.

entities.text: SPORTS FORM: HOW DOES YOUR CHILD IDENTIFY? Did you know that the sports physical forms required for Missouri kids to play school team sports come from MSHSAA (Missouri State High School Activities Association)? These standard forms now include the question: “How does your child identify?” In no way, shape, or form should “identifies as” belong on a sports physical form. It should be sex assigned at birth — period! This is about protecting fair competition and common sense. Contact the MSHSAA Board today and voice your concerns. • Jim Welby (St. Louis) — jwelby@stdominichs.org • email@mshsaa.org Or what’s next… boys competing in girls sports and vice versa? Parents — it’s time to speak up now.

entities.text: EMAIL TEMPLATE To: jwelby@stdominichs.org; email@mshsaa.orgDear MSHSAA Board of Directors,As a concerned Missouri parent, I am writing to demand the immediate removal of the question “How does your child identify?” (or any similar gender identity language) from the MSHSAA Preparticipation Physical Evaluation forms.This question has no place on a sports physical form. The only relevant medical information is sex assigned at birth — period. Introducing subjective “identity” language into a required medical clearance document is inappropriate, medically unnecessary, and highly offensive to many families who expect these forms to focus on objective health and safety, not ideology.Missouri law clearly requires participation in school sports based on biological sex. This wording undermines that law, confuses the process, and erodes parental trust. It signals that biological reality is optional — opening the door to unfair competition, including boys in girls’ sports.I urge you to revise the forms without delay to reflect biological sex only. Parents across Missouri are watching and will hold the Board accountable.Thank you for your prompt attention to this critical issue.Sincerely,

entities.text: HAPPY PARENTAL RIGHTS MONTH! On June 1, 1925, the U.S. Supreme Court issued one of the most important parental rights decisions in American history: Pierce v. Society of Sisters. The Court affirmed a principle that still matters today: "The child is not the mere creature of the State." More than a century later, parents across the country continue to advocate for a voice in their children's education and future. As we celebrate Parental Rights Month, consider supporting the work of educating, equipping, and engaging parents nationwide. Thanks to a generous partner, every donation made through June 30 will be matched dollar-for-dollar up to $40,000. https://www.momsforliberty.org/june-26-matching-grant/ #ParentalRightsMonth #WeTheParents #Moms4Liberty

entities.author: Joshua Voelkerding
entities.text: On the bullying topic that is very interesting to me as I have 2 kids in the district that have gone through (and going through) some very awkward phases that from what I knew of school, made bullying a concern for me, and not only have we not seen bullying, but have watched virtually the opposite.I am sorry for anyone who's kids are/have been bullied and would say continue to advocate for your kids in a CONSTRUCTIVE way. I will also say if you think you're going to find a school where bullying DOESN'T occur or that your kid isn't going to be exposed to something you're mistaken. As someone who went through Public (K-4) and Private (5-12) you will see the same issues either way.

entities.author: School Watchlist
entities.text: WHERE DO YOU DRAW THE LINE? Public schools should educate—not indoctrinate. • Flying sexual flags endorses adult ideologies that contradict the faith of many Christian families. • Stocking libraries with sexual and vulgar books for all ages exposes kids to inappropriate content. • Hiding books in classroom libraries keeps parents in the dark. • Threatening lawsuits to allow boys in girls’ or girls’ in boys locker rooms and restrooms violates privacy, safety, and fairness. The line is simple: Age-appropriate academics, full transparency with parents, and basic biological reality. Schools serve children and families—not activist agendas. Demand curriculum review, parental notification, and neutral education. Your voice matters.

I heard she threatened to sue the school if they passed a policy 2116 to NOT allow boys in girls restrooms and locker rooms. I also have good reason to believe she recently read a transgender surgery book to her kindergarten class. These teachers are part of the problem when their empathy for their child effects all of the district. This is how we get Transgender flags hanging throughout our hallways and young minds confused about who God made them to be. Not everyone’s child has a solid foundation of Christ and are at risk of becoming confused. Those are who I’m concerned about.

entities.text: Jessica Mikel Check this for grammar errorsThese titles have been challenged in our district because they contain graphic sexual content far beyond “tough topics.” Here are some of the direct quotes:- Crank by Ellen Hopkins (graphic rape scene):“It went, all right, with an audible tear. Pain mushroomed into agony and all I could do was go stiff. ‘You weren’t lying, you bitch!’ I laid there, sobbing…”- All Boys Aren’t Blue by George M. Johnson (explicit underage sex scene):“I put some lube on, and I got him on his knees… And I began to slide into him from behind.”These are not isolated lines - entire scenes describe masturbation, oral sex, anal sex, and sexual violence in explicit detail. Publisher “12-13-14” ratings are just marketing. Independent reviewers and most parents rate this content 16–18+.No one is “pretending these things don’t exist.” We’re saying 12 year olds shouldn’t have unrestricted access to graphic porn in written form at school without their parents’ knowledge or consent.This isn’t about shielding kids from reality- it’s about who decides when and how they’re exposed. Parents, not teachers stocking classroom libraries.I don’t think content like this should be handed to 12 year olds behind their parents’ backs? If their parents want them to have it, then their parents can get it for them.

entities.author: Jessica Mikel
entities.text: Matt Stolle the three i looked at (i can't read the title of the fourth in your photo) were rated for ages 12-13-14. And I'm not sure what your upbringing was like, but I'm pretty sure the average 12yo boy is well aware of what is happening in that scene and shouldn't be shamed for it. This isn't required reading, it's an option for a student who might not be able to identify with the other options available. I can absolutely promise you that books are not causing our children to become deviant. I have never met a criminal or teen mom that can trace their issues back to a BOOK they read in middle school. entities.author: Bryce Krawzik
entities.text: Matt Stolle, parental involvement is a vital part of education, and every parent absolutely has the right to guide their own child’s reading choices. However, there is a significant legal and ethical difference between a parent's right to guide their own child and an attempt to restrict access for the entire student body.In fact, the Francis Howell School District already has policies in place (such as the Library Opt-Out form) that allow parents to specifically restrict their own children from checking out certain materials or genres. This ensures that you have the "consent" and control you are asking for regarding your own family's boundaries.In a public district, the standard is to provide a broad range of professionally curated materials and then allow individual families to decide what is right for them. When one group of parents demands the removal of books entirely, they are effectively overriding the parental consent of other families who want their children to have access to those stories. By removing these books, the district isn't protecting parents; it is removing the choice from all parents. Public education is built on the idea that we can coexist with different values, and that requires keeping the library a space for everyone rather than a space limited by the preferences of a few.

entities.text: ARREST MADE: Fox Middle School teacher, Zachery Robert Leonard, 42, of St. Louis has been arrested and charged following an investigation into inappropriate sexual and criminal conduct involving a student under 14. Arnold Detectives along with School Resource Officers began an immediate investigation after the incident was reported on 5/6/2026. Leonard was initially arrested on 5/6/2026 but released as Detectives continued to gather evidence. On 5/11/2026 Detectives submitted a Probable Cause Statement to the Prosecuting Attorney's Office. On 5/14/2026 a No Bond Warrant was issued for Leonard's arrest and Arnold Detectives were able to locate and take him into custody without incident. Leonard has been charged with Enticement of a Child, (2x) Child Molestation 3rd Degree, and (2x) Sexual Contact w/ Student. Leonard is currently being held at the Arnold Police Department Jail without bond. We would like to thank the Fox-C6 School District for their cooperation and assistance with this investigation. We would also like to thank the Jefferson County Prosecuting Attorney's Office for moving quickly to file charges in this case. Our priority is the safety and protection of children in our community. The actions alleged in this case represent a serious breach of trust and we will continue to work closely with prosecutors to ensure accountability.

entities.text: TRANSPARENCY ISN’T HARASSMENT. PARENTAL INVOLVEMENT ISN’T EXTREMISM. If you classify bringing the TRUTH about what’s actually happening in your child’s classroom as “harassment,” then you’ve got a serious misconception about what harassment actually is. Sharing proof, of what’s being recommended or provided isn’t bullying — it’s called being an involved parent. It’s called transparency. It’s called PROTECTING KIDS and YOUR PARENTAL RIGHTS. Real harassment is trying to silence parents who dare to look inside the classroom and speak up about what they find. Real harassment is treating moms and dads like enemies for simply letting other parents know what their children are being taught and influenced. If we can’t agree on that basic principle, we’ve lost our way. What do you think — is speaking truth in your child’s education protected, or is it being twisted into something it’s not? Drop your thoughts below. #ParentalRights #EducationTransparency #KnowWhatsInTheClassroom #FHSD #FrancisHowell

entities.author: Bryce Krawzik
entities.text: Matt Stolle, your argument relies on a fundamental mischaracterization of what school libraries actually provide. Equating books that feature LGBTQ+ characters or themes with explicit adult content is a common but incorrect talking point. Having a diverse identity is not inherently adult or sexual, and these books are selected by certified professionals to be age appropriate for the students they serve. Furthermore, the term grooming has a very specific and serious definition involving predatory behavior. Using it to describe educators providing inclusive literature is both factually wrong and deeply harmful to the actual safety of children.The job of a school is indeed to teach kids to read, write, and think critically. You cannot think critically if you are shielded from the reality that diverse people exist in the world. As a student in this district, I see that these books are not about bypassing parents. They are about ensuring that every student, including those from LGBTQ+ families or those who are LGBTQ+ themselves, feels seen and safe in their learning environment. Education should be about expanding a student’s horizons and fostering empathy, which are skills that help us navigate a world full of different perspectives.It is also important to remember that this is a public school district funded by and for the entire community. Public institutions have a duty to represent all citizens, not just those who hold one specific set of beliefs. While parents have every right to guide their own children's reading choices, they do not have the right to dictate what is available to other people's children or to erase the representation of entire groups of people from a public space. If a family requires an educational environment that aligns strictly and exclusively with their personal private or religious views, that is what private education is designed for. Public education, by definition, must remain a space that reflects the full human experience and respects the rights of every student to feel included.

entities.text: resorting to personal insults and age-based dismissals only highlights the fact that you cannot provide a factual or evidence-based rebuttal to the points I’ve raised regarding student health and education. While you focus on where I might live or how much you think I have to learn, I am focusing on the documented well-being of our community's youth and the professional standards of our educational system. Dismissive comments do not change the clinical consensus of the American Psychological Association, nor do they invalidate the necessity of inclusive resources for children who are currently struggling to feel safe in their schools. If you had a substantive argument against the mental health benefits of representation or the legal obligations of public libraries, you would have presented it by now. Instead, you've chosen to ignore the human impact of these policies to focus on "winning" a social media exchange. I am happy to continue this conversation if you ever decide to address the actual safety and developmental needs of the students involved, but until then, your refusal to engage with the facts speaks much louder than any insult could. Try again hun

entities.text: Carrie Johnson dismissing the lived experiences of students with a single word doesn’t change the overwhelming consensus from the American Psychological Association and the American Academy of Pediatrics, both of which recognize that children can and do identify as part of the LGBTQ+ community from a young age. Claiming that representation is wrong ignores the clinical reality that access to age appropriate, inclusive literature is a vital protective factor against the high rates of depression, anxiety, and suicidal ideation that marginalized youth face when they are isolated. These books are not about adult themes but are curated tools that provide children with the language to understand their own emotions and foster empathy for their peers, which is a foundational goal of any public education system. Furthermore, public school libraries are legally and ethically obligated to serve the entire student body, not just the viewpoints of one specific group. Denying the existence of these children or removing their access to information does not stop them from being LGBTQ+, it only ensures they feel unsafe and unsupported in their own community. True education is about preparing all children to navigate a diverse world with kindness and factual understanding rather than fear and exclusion.
