entities.text: Jane Puszkar it is important to clarify that in the state of Missouri, School Library Media Specialists are not merely individuals with a few college credits. They are certified educators who are typically required to hold a Master’s degree in Library Science or a related field. These professionals are highly trained in information literacy, curriculum support, and child development, and their primary goal is to ensure that every student has access to accurate information that reflects the diverse world we live in. Dismissing the scientific and legal reality of this issue because it challenges your personal worldview does not change the clinical facts regarding gender dysphoria or the documented necessity of representation. When you ignore the guidance of the American Psychological Association and the American Academy of Pediatrics, you are choosing personal opinion over the peer reviewed evidence that proves inclusive literature serves as a protective factor against depression and self harm for marginalized youth. Education is not a zero sum game where including one group takes away from another; it is about providing a safe and supportive environment for every single child. If you truly value the standard of professionalism you mentioned, I would encourage you to read the full context of why these resources are deemed essential by the world's leading medical and psychological experts rather than dismissing the very people dedicated to student success and safety.

entities.author: Bryce Krawzik
entities.text: Jane Puszkar, I strongly encourage you to look beyond your personal perspective and examine the actual consensus within the fields of adolescent psychology, medical science, and constitutional law. By labeling inclusive literature as an agenda or pornography, you are fundamentally mischaracterizing age appropriate educational resources that serve as a critical lifeline for students. To be clear, these books are curated by professionals to reflect diverse identities rather than to provide graphic content. Equating the existence of LGBTQ+ people to pornography is a harmful falsehood that ignores the reality of human identity and creates a dangerous environment for marginalized students. For a child experiencing gender dysphoria, access to this literature is a vital mental health resource that provides the language needed to understand their emotions, which is essential for healthy self regulation and development. According to the American Psychological Association and the American Academy of Pediatrics, the lack of representation and social support in schools is a direct contributor to the alarmingly high rates of depression, anxiety, and self harm among LGBTQ+ youth. Providing these books is quite literally a matter of suicide prevention and overall student safety. Furthermore, restricting access to information in public institutions often borders on a violation of First Amendment rights and ignores the fact that public school libraries must serve the entire community rather than just one specific viewpoint. These stories also benefit cisgender and straight students by fostering empathy and teaching them how to coexist in a diverse society, which is a necessary skill for the modern workforce. When you deny children the ability to see themselves or their peers reflected in their education, you are not protecting them from an imaginary threat. Instead, you are isolating vulnerable kids and creating a culture of shame that leads to long term psychological trauma. Understanding the truth requires looking at the human impact of these policies and recognizing that every child, regardless of their background or identity, deserves to feel seen, safe, and supported in their learning environment.

entities.text: PARENTS: WAKE UP ON SOCIAL EMOTIONAL LEARNING! Just received this email from the Character Strong program, which is implemented throughout the Francis Howell School District. They’re doubling down next year — pushing Tier 2 small groups and Tier 3 one-on-one interventions for kids’ “MENTAL HEALTH NEEDS.” Social Emotional Learning is now front and center… while academics take a backseat. Real question: If kids need this much emotional intervention at school, isn’t the real problem at HOME? Broken families, no structure, endless screens, checked-out parents? We’re treating symptoms with expensive programs instead of fixing the root. How do we actually solve this where it starts — in the home? Thoughts? Speak up before next year. EMAIL: Board@FHSDSchools.org

entities.author: Elizabeth Davie
entities.text: Question: shouldn't parents know what the content is before they challenge it? These are just blurbs about a book. I could write a blurb about the movie "Mrs Doubtfire" like this: "Daniel Hillard was in a tough spot. The terms of the divorce made it clear that he would have no unsupervised time with his children. But when he saw an ad for a nanny for his children, he knew he'd do anything to get his children back. Even if it includes disguising himself as a safe and sweet elderly woman, running an elaborate ruse, lying to his children, and even harming his ex-wife's new boyfriend. What would you do when you lose the ones you love?"I've read "A Long Way Down." Not only is it long-form poetry, a genre that many students would not otherwise be exposed to, but it goes into the mind of a young preteen/teen who has been put in an impossible position through no control of his own and must decide what is right and what is wrong for himself. It's great to think that all kids are always innocent, but that simply isn't true. Reading books about characters that they can relate to is an incredibly meaningful way to start making sense of things that have happened that are beyond their control and a safe way to help kids who are fortunate enough not to have experienced hard things to develop empathy. Also, the philosophical questions that arise from books about war and dystopian societies and some of the other subjects above can be a creative, engaging, and eye-opening path to explore critical thinking.

entities.author: Bryce Krawzik
entities.text: Jane Puszkar I am a student, not a 'troll in a basement.' My 'keyboard' is the same one I use to text my friends and family, complete my schoolwork, advocate for my peers, and manage my job. Dismissing my voice because of my age or living situation doesn't change the reality of the students I see every day.Regarding the library: access to diverse information is not 'indoctrination.' Many students deal with feelings they don't understand, and seeing themselves represented in literature can be lifesaving. Being LGBTQ+ isn't an 'agenda' you can talk someone into; it’s an identity. Showcasing these books is simply a reminder that LGBTQ+ people are human beings who deserve the same respect as anyone else. We breathe the same air and bleed the same blood.Furthermore, I am not the one causing division; I am responding to the division you have already created. You have publicly supported rhetoric that targets marginalized groups, including calling all undocumented immigrants 'criminals.' While legal status is a complex issue, labeling people that way ignores the fact that most are families seeking safety through a flawed and difficult system.If you truly want what’s best for all students, you should be willing to listen to us rather than insulting us. I’m out here every day living the reality of this school district. You are a horrible example of a human being and I hope one day you can come to peace with everyone aside from their ethnicity, sexuality, religion and or background. And thank you I will be having a nice day knowing I have a voice and I get to use it to protect students from people like you.

entities.text: Jane Puszkar from what I read of the article linked in this post, and no other background about this particular teacher, my takeaway was that she was being singled out for something happening in her personal life between her and her child. I know nothing about how this teacher interacts with school politics or if she even shares her personal politics with her students, as the article was nothing about that. Can you please point to me the part of the linked article that has anything to do with her threatening to sue the district? What does that have to do with the article about her child losing access to medical support previously provided? I'm just not following. And if you want to question my conservative values I'm happy to meet with you for a coffee or lunch and we can discuss. I personally don't think it's biblical for parents to affirm a transgender child but I also am comfortable enough in how I'm training up my children in Christ's word that I don't feel I need to attack a teacher because she is parenting a different way than I do, and I would not be concerned having her as a teacher of any of my own children as long as she is able to teach my child the subject of the class and shows my children kindness and compassion, which from the comments, it sound like she is a very kind teacher who knows her subject. Please please help connect the dots from the article linked in the post to boys in girls bathrooms and suing the district. I'm just not seeing it.

entities.text: SCHOOLS DON’T NEED TO VALIDATE STUDENT IDENTITIES TO PROTECT THEM. If a student is being bullied, the priority should be stopping the bullying behavior. That means addressing the individuals responsible, enforcing consequences, and creating a safe learning environment. The focus should be on fixing the problem, not reframing it. Schools don't need to validate or categorize a student's personal identity in order to protect them. They need to ensure that no student is mistreated.

entities.text: The receipts are in. If you are a teacher who has ever written a dues check and assumed it was going toward better pay, stronger benefits, or a decent contract, read carefully. A new report from Defending Education has blown the lid off one of the most brazen political money machines in American history, and your money is in it.Since August 2015, the National Education Association (NEA) and the American Federation of Teachers (AFT) have funneled a combined $669,324,912.33 in member dues and PAC funds into left-wing political entities, far-left nonprofits, and Democratic campaigns. Fold in state and local affiliates, and the total surpasses $1 billion.The big money tells the story. The State Engagement Fund, a Democratic Party infrastructure vehicle, received $60,525,000. The For Our Future Action Fund took $44,732,078. The Senate Majority PAC received $32,655,000. The House Majority PAC got $25,842,790. The Strategic Victory Fund, created in 2020 explicitly to defeat Donald Trump, received $19,300,000.On top of all that, the unions pumped over $85 million directly into Democrat Party entities at every level of government, not counting a single dollar in individual candidate contributions. The Biden Victory Fund received $923,500. The Hillary Victory Fund got $444,250. The Bill, Hillary, and Chelsea Clinton Foundation collected $725,000, with another $400,000 to the Clinton Global Initiative.https://redstate.com/ben-smith/2026/04/29/teachers-dues-became-a-1b-democrat-slush-fundnot-classroom-funding-n2201843

entities.author: Amy Mallams
entities.text: Transgender People Are NOT a Threat to Public SafetyAnti-trans rhetoric portrays transgender people as violent, predatory, and/or hypersexual. In reality, transgender people are far more likely to experience harassment and violence than to inflict harm on others. Myths about transgender people often fall into two main categories: 1.) claims that transgender people are inherently violent 2.) claims that transgender people are sexual predators. NEITHER of these claims is supported by evidence. Instead, such false narratives distort public perception and fuel policies that put transgender communities in danger. These false narratives are not just misunderstandings; they are part of what scholars call a moral panic. Moral panic is when fear is exaggerated and directed at a marginalized group, painting them as a threat to society. Moral panics recycle old stigmas and anxieties (usually about race, gender, or sexuality) to justify discrimination and criminalization.Scholars note that moral panics often emerge as a response to social change; a way for communities to make sense of changing norms or perceived threats to traditional values. Throughout U.S. history, “protect the children” rhetoric has been used to vilify different groups: casting Black men as threats to white women,branding gay men as predators, and nowportraying transgender people as dangerous in schools and public bathrooms. These myths follow the same pattern, weaponizing fear to roll back civil rights under the guise of safety.Are transgender people a threat to public safety?NO. There is NO evidence that transgender people are more likely to engage in violent or criminal behavior than cisgender people. Research conducted on criminology and public safety consistently shows that gender identity does NOT predict criminal behavior. Studies find NO evidence that transgender people commit crimes at higher rates than cisgender people; instead, transgender people are more likely to experience discrimination and over-policing, facing disproportionate surveillance and punishment by law enforcement even when NO offense has been committed.According to the Bureau of Justice Statistics, transgender people were four times more likely to be victimized by violent crimes than cisgender people. Studies also document that transgender individuals experience disproportionately high rates of harassment, intimate violence, and hate crimes compared to cisgender people.These patterns show that transgender communities are far more vulnerable to violence, NOT more likely to commit it.These findings extend to public spaces, especially bathrooms. Studies consistently find that gender-inclusive restrooms and nondiscrimination policies do NOT compromise safety. In fact, places that have passed inclusive bathroom laws remain just as safe as they were before and had NO rise in crime or misconduct. Conversely, evidence shows that transgender people are at greater risk in bathrooms and other public facilities. Research from numerous medical, legal, and policy organizations consistently finds that gender-inclusive restrooms and nondiscrimination policies do NOT compromise safety. Many transgender people avoid public bathrooms altogether, leading to health problems, missed school, and limited participation in daily life.As Woodhull emphasized in testimony opposing Montana’s HB 121, bathroom bans do NOT make anyone safer; they increase harassment of everyone, force people into unsafe conditions, and violate basic rights to dignity and privacy. These laws and stereotypes isolate transgender people from public life, increase vulnerability to violence, and shift attention away from the real issue: transgender people’s basic right to safety, dignity, and access to public spaces.Are transgender people hypersexual or predatory?NO. Research does NOT suggest that transgender people are hypersexual or more likely to be sexually aggressive.Research shows that transgender folks are NOT more likely than cisgender people to sexually hurt or exploit others. In fact, research shows that transgender people are often the ones getting sexually assaulted. The U.S. Transgender Survey found that 47% of respondents had been sexually assaulted at some point. To put that in perspective, about 19.3% of cisgender women and 1.7% of cisgender men experience sexual violence in their lifetime. Despite being feared as predators, transgender people are far more likely to be victims of abuse and exploitation.The “predatory” framing does more than misrepresent reality: it legitimizes harmful policies and fuels harassment. Incorrect framings of transgender individuals as fundamentally dangerous or abnormal are used to justify increased surveillance of transgender people, keeping them out of certain public areas, and limiting their access to healthcare. For example, Texas Republican Senator Ted Cruz warned that allowing transgender people to use bathrooms matching their gender identity would be “opening the door for predators,” claiming that such laws would let “any man enter a women’s restroom, a little girl’s restroom and stay there.” This rhetoric directly ties trans inclusion to threats against women and children, echoing the same moral panic used against earlier marginalized groups.Rather than protecting communities, this myth perpetuates stigma and violence against transgender people. The stereotype that transgender people are hypersexual or predatory plays on long-standing fears about women’s safety. Throughout history, claims that marginalized groups were sexually dangerous have been used to justify exclusion and violence — first against Black men, then gay men, and now transgender people. Not only does this lead policymakers to overlook the needs of transgender people, but it also overlooks real actual threats to women, children, and other marginalized people.Policy Recommendations1.) Reject bathroom bans.Restricting restroom access harms public health, increases harassment, and violates basic human rights to dignity and privacy. Policies that ensure gender-inclusive restrooms and nondiscrimination protections reduce stigma, improve safety, and affirm the humanity of all people.2.) Affirm access to safe public spaces.Policies that provide gender-inclusive restrooms and nondiscrimination protections, such as ensuring access to single-stall facilities in schools, workplaces, and transportation hubs, reduce harassment and support the health and well-being of all individuals.3.) Protect dignity, privacy, & rights.Bathroom bans undermine the human rights to privacy and personal dignity. By singling out transgender people for surveillance and exclusion, they erode trust in public institutions and create unsafe conditions for everyone. Protecting access to public facilities is not only a matter of health, but also a matter of fundamental human rights.4.) Promote education & awareness.Misinformation about transgender people fuels stigma, hate, discrimination and violence. Public education campaigns, inclusive school curricula, and professional training can help counter such harmful myths. These interventions reduce prejudice, build safer communities, and affirm the dignity of transgender people. In addition, funding more research on gender diversity and inclusion can help policymakers make evidence-based decisions rather than relying on fear or misinformation.https://www.woodhullfoundation.org/fact-checked/transgender-people-are-not-a-threat-to-public-safety/

Many transgender people avoid public bathrooms altogether, leading to health problems, missed school, and limited participation in daily life.As Woodhull emphasized in testimony opposing Montana’s HB 121, bathroom bans do NOT make anyone safer; they increase harassment of everyone, force people into unsafe conditions, and violate basic rights to dignity and privacy. These laws and stereotypes isolate transgender people from public life, increase vulnerability to violence, and shift attention away from the real issue: transgender people’s basic right to safety, dignity, and access to public spaces.Are transgender people hypersexual or predatory?NO. Research does NOT suggest that transgender people are hypersexual or more likely to be sexually aggressive.Research shows that transgender folks are NOT more likely than cisgender people to sexually hurt or exploit others. In fact, research shows that transgender people are often the ones getting sexually assaulted. The U.S. Transgender Survey found that 47% of respondents had been sexually assaulted at some point. To put that in perspective, about 19.3% of cisgender women and 1.7% of cisgender men experience sexual violence in their lifetime. Despite being feared as predators, transgender people are far more likely to be victims of abuse and exploitation.The “predatory” framing does more than misrepresent reality: it legitimizes harmful policies and fuels harassment. Incorrect framings of transgender individuals as fundamentally dangerous or abnormal are used to justify increased surveillance of transgender people, keeping them out of certain public areas, and limiting their access to healthcare. For example, Texas Republican Senator Ted Cruz warned that allowing transgender people to use bathrooms matching their gender identity would be “opening the door for predators,” claiming that such laws would let “any man enter a women’s restroom, a little girl’s restroom and stay there.” This rhetoric directly ties trans inclusion to threats against women and children, echoing the same moral panic used against earlier marginalized groups.Rather than protecting communities, this myth perpetuates stigma and violence against transgender people. The stereotype that transgender people are hypersexual or predatory plays on long-standing fears about women’s safety. Throughout history, claims that marginalized groups were sexually dangerous have been used to justify exclusion and violence — first against Black men, then gay men, and now transgender people. Not only does this lead policymakers to overlook the needs of transgender people, but it also overlooks real actual threats to women, children, and other marginalized people.Policy Recommendations1.) Reject bathroom bans.Restricting restroom access harms public health, increases harassment, and violates basic human rights to dignity and privacy. Policies that ensure gender-inclusive restrooms and nondiscrimination protections reduce stigma, improve safety, and affirm the humanity of all people.2.) Affirm access to safe public spaces.Policies that provide gender-inclusive restrooms and nondiscrimination protections, such as ensuring access to single-stall facilities in schools, workplaces, and transportation hubs, reduce harassment and support the health and well-being of all individuals.3.) Protect dignity, privacy, & rights.Bathroom bans undermine the human rights to privacy and personal dignity. By singling out transgender people for surveillance and exclusion, they erode trust in public institutions and create unsafe conditions for everyone. Protecting access to public facilities is not only a matter of health, but also a matter of fundamental human rights.4.) Promote education & awareness.Misinformation about transgender people fuels stigma, hate, discrimination and violence. Public education campaigns, inclusive school curricula, and professional training can help counter such harmful myths. These interventions reduce prejudice, build safer communities, and affirm the dignity of transgender people. In addition, funding more research on gender diversity and inclusion can help policymakers make evidence-based decisions rather than relying on fear or misinformation.https://www.woodhullfoundation.org/fact-checked/transgender-people-are-not-a-threat-to-public-safety/

entities.text: Kerry Baider listen, uninformed voting is stupid and I agree with you on that, but that’s not all 82% who didn’t vote in April. I guarantee you if you just went around and asked people would tell you they had no idea an election even happened. That’s voter disenfranchisement. entities.author: School Watchlist
entities.text: The Missouri NEA (teachers’ union) sued the state of Missouri. They tried to stop $50+ million in public tax money from going to the MOScholars program — a scholarship that helps certain kids (especially those with disabilities or from low-income families) pay for private school, homeschooling, tutoring, or therapy. The NEA argued the funding was done the wrong way (unconstitutional) and would hurt public schools. The judge dismissed the lawsuit completely. He ruled the NEA didn’t have the legal right to sue in this way, and even if they did, the funding was legal. The money can keep flowing to the scholarships.

entities.author: Christen Pierce
entities.text: When I had the opportunity to sit on the review committee for this video, I was grateful for the chance to participate in FHSD’s materials review process. I’m commenting here because I find it very disingenuous to claim that it was “voted to retain by a full liberal committee” when the “full committee” did not return to participate in the vote. On the day that we met to discuss and vote on the video, I was surprised to see that (still active at the time) School Board Director Jane Puszkar did not join us to discuss her concerns about the video, if she had any. It is important for our community to note that choosing not to participate does not mean conservative voices were left out of the discussion. I have five kids and I care deeply about the things they are exposed to; in this case, I do believe that retention was the right choice. If you have any genuine questions about why I voted the way I did, I’m happy to discuss my thoughts about it.

entities.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | BREAKING ANOTHER school settles! Kathy McCord, an Indiana school counselor with 37 years in education, reached a nearly $200,000 settlement ($195,000 for damages, attorneys' fees, and costs) with South Madison Community School Corporation after the district fired her for speaking to a journalist about its gender identity policy. The policy directed staff to use students' preferred names and pronouns without notifying or obtaining consent from parents — and in some cases to keep that information secret from them. HUGE WIN for parental rights and free speech! #jesus #school #FreeSpeech #parents #education #WinBig | EfyUgmj.com

As a conservative speaking to another conservative, take this crap down! (And to my liberal, progressive friends, please don't let this lead you to believe all conservatives are like this!)

entities.author: Lindsey Scheller
entities.text: Just FYI: when my son was in fourth grade, he had recently been diagnosed with dyslexia and was falling behind in reading. As a mom and as a teacher, I was devastated. I hired Mrs. Becky Hormuth as a tutor for him over the summer. Let me tell you some of the ways she “influenced him.” ￼She taught him a bunch of reading strategies. ￼She made him feel more confident as a reader. She convinced him that being dyslexic was nothing to be embarrassed by. She got him hooked up with high interest books that encouraged him to read more. She made it fun so he wanted to go see her, even over the summer. She made him believe that he was capable of anything he wanted to do. And now he’s a thriving ninth grader with a A in English class. This post is gross.

entities.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | Becky Hormuth and her transgender son, Levi, thought they were protected after a Missouri law banning transition-related care for minors took effect in August. The law grandfathered in those who had already been receiving puberty blockers or hormone therapy prior to Aug. 28, meaning they, in theory, would be able to continue their treatment. However, the hospital where Levi had been receiving care informed patients in September that it would no longer be providing such care, citing the “unsustainable liability” the law creates for health care professionals, as it allows providers of transition-related care for minors to be sued by their patients. “We both just sat and cried together on the floor of his bedroom,” Becky said of the reaction she and Levi had upon hearing the news. “He connected with those doctors, and they’re like family to us — they know him personally. His big worry was, ‘Who’s going to help me now?’” ​​More than 500 state bills targeting lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender and queer people have been introduced in 2023, according to a tally by the American Civil Liberties Union. Of those bills, 75 became law, according to an NBC News analysis of the ACLU’s data. Read more: nbcnews.app.link/xHnIJsCtDFb | WdaypvBaRA.com

entities.text: Move St. Charles County School Board Elections to November for Higher Turnout￼ Missouri Senate Bill 1002 would move St. Charles County school board elections and tax increase votes to the November general election for much higher voter turnout. Sponsored by Senator Adam Schnelting, the bill has passed the Senate and is now in the House. Why this is a win for parents and taxpayers: • April 7 turnout was only 19% — a tiny fraction of voters decided the entire Francis Howell School Board. • November elections typically see 60-70%+ turnout, giving everyday families a real voice instead of letting special interests dominate. - For example special interests (including teachers’ unions like the MNEA/NEA) are actively organizing to kill the bill so they can keep low-turnout April elections that favor organized special interests. • School board decisions affect our kids and millions in taxes — they deserve broad community input, not low-turnout insider control. • This puts power back where it belongs: with parents and taxpayers. This isn’t partisanship — it’s basic democracy and accountability. =============================== Call or email your Missouri State Representative TODAY and tell them to SUPPORT SB 1002. =============================== Always include your full address to confirm you’re a constituent. • Tricia Byrnes (District 63 – Wentzville area)�Email: Tricia.Byrnes@house.mo.gov�Phone: (573) 751-1460 • Deanna Self (District 64 – parts of O’Fallon, St. Paul, etc.)�Email: Deanna.Self@house.mo.gov�Phone: (573) 751-1484 • Wendy Hausman (District 65 – St. Peters, Cottleville, parts of St. Charles)�Email: Wendy.Hausman@house.mo.gov�Phone: (573) 751-3717 • Scott Miller (District 69 – additional St. Charles County areas overlapping FHSD)�Email: Scott.Miller@house.mo.gov�Phone: (573) 751-5365 • Terri Violet (District 104 – parts of St. Charles County / FHSD)�Email: Terri.Violet@house.mo.gov • Travis Wilson (District 106 – St. Charles area)�Use the contact form on house.mo.gov/MemberDetails.aspx?district=106 (no public direct email listed). • CC - adam.schnelting@senate.mo.gov, nick.schroer@senate.mo.gov

entities.author: School Watchlist is with State Senator Nick Schroer.
entities.text: Francis Howell Parents — Momentum is on our side! This week, the Eighth Circuit Court of Appeals delivered a major win for parents and taxpayers. The court ruled that authors and publishers do not have a right to force sexually explicit materials into public school libraries. The case involved Iowa’s SF 496, which requires age-appropriate books and removes materials depicting sex acts. The court made it clear: • The First Amendment does not guarantee any book at taxpayer expense. • Removing explicit content is not a “book ban.” Missouri parents, it’s time to act. Age-inappropriate and sexually explicit materials still don’t belong in our kids’ schools — especially in elementary and middle grades. Contact our St. Charles County senators today and urge them to introduce or support strong legislation like Iowa’s SF 496 (and back SB 483 sponsored by Sen. Nick Schroer to protect kids from explicit sexual material): Use the email draft below. The more voices, the stronger the message. Our kids’ innocence and education come first. Share with other FHSD parents! #FrancisHowell #ProtectOurKids #ParentalRights #SB483 ———————————————————————— Email Draft (Copy & Paste Ready) To: adam.schnelting@senate.mo.gov, nick.schroer@senate.mo.gov Subject: Remove Age-Inappropriate Materials from Missouri Schools Dear Senator Schnelting and Senator Schroer, I am a parent in the Francis Howell School District in St. Charles County. I urge you to champion legislation similar to Iowa’s SF 496 and to support SB 483 (sponsored by Sen. Schroer) to strengthen protections against explicit sexual material in schools. Recent rulings, including this week’s Eighth Circuit decision, confirm that schools have the authority and responsibility to keep age-inappropriate books — especially those depicting or describing sex acts — out of classrooms and libraries, particularly for K-6 students. Parents deserve transparency and the right to protect their children’s innocence. Taxpayer-funded schools should focus on education, not exposing kids to explicit content. Please take the lead on this issue in the next legislative session. I would appreciate any update on your plans to protect Missouri families. Thank you for your strong advocacy for St. Charles County families. Sincerely,

Contact our St. Charles County senators today and urge them to introduce or support strong legislation like Iowa’s SF 496 (and back SB 483 sponsored by Sen. Nick Schroer to protect kids from explicit sexual material): Use the email draft below. The more voices, the stronger the message. Our kids’ innocence and education come first. Share with other FHSD parents! #FrancisHowell #ProtectOurKids #ParentalRights #SB483 ———————————————————————— Email Draft (Copy & Paste Ready) To: adam.schnelting@senate.mo.gov, nick.schroer@senate.mo.gov Subject: Remove Age-Inappropriate Materials from Missouri Schools Dear Senator Schnelting and Senator Schroer, I am a parent in the Francis Howell School District in St. Charles County. I urge you to champion legislation similar to Iowa’s SF 496 and to support SB 483 (sponsored by Sen. Schroer) to strengthen protections against explicit sexual material in schools. Recent rulings, including this week’s Eighth Circuit decision, confirm that schools have the authority and responsibility to keep age-inappropriate books — especially those depicting or describing sex acts — out of classrooms and libraries, particularly for K-6 students. Parents deserve transparency and the right to protect their children’s innocence. Taxpayer-funded schools should focus on education, not exposing kids to explicit content. Please take the lead on this issue in the next legislative session. I would appreciate any update on your plans to protect Missouri families. Thank you for your strong advocacy for St. Charles County families. Sincerely, See less

entities.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | Becky Hormuth and her transgender son, Levi, thought they were protected after a Missouri law banning transition-related care for minors took effect in August. The law grandfathered in those who had already been receiving puberty blockers or hormone therapy prior to Aug. 28, meaning they, in theory, would be able to continue their treatment. However, the hospital where Levi had been receiving care informed patients in September that it would no longer be providing such care, citing the “unsustainable liability” the law creates for health care professionals, as it allows providers of transition-related care for minors to be sued by their patients. “We both just sat and cried together on the floor of his bedroom,” Becky said of the reaction she and Levi had upon hearing the news. “He connected with those doctors, and they’re like family to us — they know him personally. His big worry was, ‘Who’s going to help me now?’” ​​More than 500 state bills targeting lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender and queer people have been introduced in 2023, according to a tally by the American Civil Liberties Union. What schools are you considering (or avoiding) for your kids? —our children’s future depends on it. #CollegeChoices #HigherEducation #ParentalResponsibility

entities.text: Wentzville School District Settles Transgender Bathroom Lawsuit with Missouri AG Great news for transparency and parental rights in Wentzville R-IV Schools! The district has reached a settlement with Attorney General Catherine Hanaway, resolving a 2023 Sunshine Law case. The board was accused of discussing a transgender student bathroom and locker room access policy in closed sessions (June 2023) instead of openly with the public. Key points of the April 2026 agreement: • No admission of wrongdoing by the district • Acknowledges parents’ fundamental right to know about and participate in decisions affecting their children’s education, safety, and welfare • Commits to full compliance with Missouri’s Open Meetings/Sunshine Law • Requires Sunshine Law training for board members and staff • Must post a public statement about the case and settlement on the district website This reinforces that important school policies should be debated in the open, not behind closed doors. Full settlement: https://ago.mo.gov/.../State-v.-Wentzville-Settlement... What do you think—transparency wins? Share your thoughts!

entities.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | The Supreme Court has ruled that parents cannot be forced to have their young children participate in school lessons that conflict with their sincerely held religious beliefs. The Court said schools must allow families to opt their children out of certain elementary classroom materials involving LGBTQ themes when those materials contradict their faith. The case arose after a Maryland school district removed opt-out options and stopped notifying parents about the content being taught. The ruling does not ban the material itself, but it affirms a foundational principle: parents — not the state — have the primary responsibility for directing the moral and religious upbringing of their children. Schools may teach these topics, but they cannot compel participation from students whose families object on religious grounds. | UOoAA.com

entities.text: Teacher wins $650,000 lawsuit after refusing to use trans students’ preferred pronouns A former Indiana music teacher has been awarded a $650,000 settlement following a long-running legal dispute with his school district over classroom pronoun use. The case began in 2017 when the teacher said his religious beliefs prevented him from using students’ preferred pronouns, leading to a policy conflict with school administrators and eventually a civil rights lawsuit. In response, the teacher adopted a last-name-only approach for all students as a compromise. However, some students reported feeling singled out and uncomfortable, prompting the school district to withdraw the arrangement. The disagreement escalated, ultimately resulting in the teacher’s resignation and years of legal proceedings over claims of religious discrimination. The settlement concludes a seven-year case that has drawn national attention to the balance between religious rights and student inclusion in schools. The outcome reflects ongoing legal debates in the United States over how institutions handle conflicts between personal beliefs and policies designed to support diverse student identities. #fblifestyle #photography #community #Education #LegalCase #USSchools References: BBC News: Coverage on education and religious rights cases Reuters: Reports on US civil rights and school disputes CNN: Analysis of pronoun policies in schools Fox News: Legal updates on education-related lawsuits

entities.author: School Watchlist
entities.text: All this outrage about schools, fire, libraries, and disability programs losing funding seems to show up only when taxpayers ask questions and say no more taxes we are tapped out. •Where is that same outrage when developers receive tax abatements and incentives that divert revenue away from our same districts? • St. Charles County’s 2024 incentive report confirms Chapter 100 and Chapter 353 abatements reduce or redirect tax dollars from schools and other local taxing authorities. • In WSD, the 2023 agreement tied to the Bryan Road/Highway N and Feise/Bryan developments includes abatement of real property taxes, with only a $50,000 annual contribution (2024–2036) instead of full taxation. But we just keep building, thousands of new homes and apartments: The Solstice The Sullivan (LSL) New Town expansion (St Charles) Shady Creek (Hwy N) Autumn Hollows (Hwy N) Creekside at Sommers (45 homes across LHS) Inverness (Bryan & Feise) The Prairie & Prairie Encore (190 apartments) Trailside Farms (Hwy N toward LSL) • Are these developments paying their full share, or are incentives shifting that burden to the community? When local officials approve these deals, they are choosing to reduce or delay full tax collections through abatements and other agreements. • Why do developers get tax breaks, while the families already living here pay the increases every year? Before asking taxpayers for more and more money, there should be accountability, transparency, and better long-term planning.

entities.author: Anelise Mossinghoff
entities.text: Prop RT may seem to be a good thing, until you look beyond the short-sighted rhetoric in favor of this. Look at the bigger picture...Think of it this way ...what would you say if your employer said that you will have a pay freeze forever going forward? What would you do about cost of living increases? What about inflation? How will you make up for those increases? It will be impossible. This is what Prop RT will do to the community. Prop RT will devastate schools, fire departments, etc...and any other organization that relies on property taxes for their funding. Where will the shortfall come from? Although Prop RT is not claiming to totally get rid of income tax, one of the suggestions is to increase sales tax. This will make those struggling with buying groceries or ANY goods and services increasingly more difficult to sustain themselves. See the picture below.

entities.author: Megan Dolphy Terrell
entities.text: You make this sound like it's required reading for kindergarten, but it's a standard middle school short story. Middle school and high school literature classes have a lot of pieces that make these 12-18 year olds think critically and that dangers can exist. Edgar Allen Poe, The Lottery, and Twilight zone scripts all have "scary" aspects. And all of them are so not realistic that I have never known a kid to be scared by them. Realistic fiction where best friends move away, dogs die, and parents get injured or leave effects kids more! But all of these kinds of literature helps people learn how to be better problem solvers, deal with difficult times, and develop as a better person with stronger emotional regulation. And they learn these things without having to actually live through the trauma. It's actually a very positive thing.

Even with many challenges, age-inappropriate books are still in our libraries, and Policy 6310 is making it nearly impossible for parents to protect our children from explicit material. We need your voices at public comments! The Workplace Culture Survey results and the vote on the new Safe Schools Curriculum are pushing further into the gender ideology movement — the wrong decision for our students and for parents trying to uphold their religious and moral beliefs. If you’re a Christian, conservative, or simply care about protecting our children, stand up and speak out. Support Jane Puszkar Jane Puszkar, FHSD Board of Education as she continues to fight for what’s right for our kids! Attend in person or watch live on the Francis Howell YouTube channel. Your presence matters now more than ever! entities.text: So I don’t think you actually read that policy, or maybe you just didn’t understand it. Having a flag in the classroom isn’t exactly part of the curriculum or a classroom discussion. Now the First Amendment, on the other hand. I’m sure you’ve read that one in its entirety. The first Amendment not only protects people’s freedom of speech, expression and religion, but also protects people (and children) from others enforcing their religious beliefs on them. For example, caring more about a piece of cloth hanging in a classroom stating this is a safe place just because your religion doesn’t agree with it.If anyone is breaking any policies…it’s this Facebook page. And it’s crazy that this page is so upset about teachers being inclusive and safe for kids when there’s been quite a few religious leaders that have been caught as pedophiles. Maybe leave the religious stuff at home instead of a public school. Or might I suggest a private school instead? You’re making it incredibly unsafe for others in your community with your blatant hatred. hope that helps!

entities.author: School Watchlist
entities.text: PRIVATE PRIDE Libraries In Classrooms I recently discovered “private pride libraries” in our 7th grade English class at Hollenbeck Middle School. Some of these books were not found in the library commons, so they appear to be in direct violation of the In-Classroom Library Policy (under 6310/6341). This policy requires all books to be provided in a list to the Board for review and prohibits bringing in books not already in the district library. This isn’t happening — unauthorized books are everywhere, the superintendent knows, and nothing’s being done. This also violates my rights as a parent, as I am unable to monitor or consent to what my child is reading in class. Violation Scenario If a classroom library includes books not reported or approved via the Learning Commons process, the teacher (or district) is in violation: • They bypassed the required transparency steps, since new titles aren’t disclosed to the Board. • They may also be subject to challenges under Policy 6341, which treats classroom and school library materials identically. [go.boarddocs.com] – Please email your concerns to Board@fhsdschools.org #SchoolTransparency #ParentalRights #FHSD #FrancisHowell #AgeAppropriateEducation

entities.author: Libby Settle
entities.text: Conversations about moving towards 1:1 device pushes in today’s day and age continues to baffle me. A quick search shows districts who have had this model are moving away from a 1:1 device often transitioning from "take-home" models to "in-class only" use or scaling back for younger students.Wake County Public School System (North Carolina): The district is moving to end its 1:1 take-home program for its 160,000 students, citing unsustainable long-term costs and the need to prioritize facilities.Fresno Unified School District (California): Starting in 2026, roughly 40,000 elementary students must return their laptops to be used exclusively at school.Charles County Public Schools (Maryland): Beginning in the 2025–26 school year, the district is overhauling its technology approach by shifting to shared devices for elementary grades and restricting individual devices to in-school use only for grades 3–8.Arlington Public Schools (Virginia): This district has scaled back its iPad program, ending take-home access for certain grade levels to reduce screen time and address parent concerns.Denver Public Schools (Colorado): While maintaining some technology, the district has significantly cut hundreds of ed-tech tools to save money and reduce data vulnerability.Kansas School Districts: Select schools in Kansas have ended individual Chromebook assignments specifically to combat excessive screen time. The concerns listed in this post are valid and utilize a considerable amount of a budget that can be reallocated to school repairs, teacher retention, updated curriculums, etc.

entities.author: School Watchlist
entities.text: SHINY NEW TECH I feel this view oversimplifies the 1:1 Chromebook push at our schools and skips key details. Valid Concerns: 1. Device Shortfalls: They’re underestimating needs—ignoring breakage, theft, or loss. We’ll need way more than the initial estimate! 2. Tech Support Gap: No plans to add to the 25 Tech Aids or place them in schools. Teachers will end up as IT fixers, stealing time from teaching. 3. Unclear Usage: Just “strategic teaching” as the reason? No details on apps, integration, or curriculum fit. 4. Data Privacy Missing: Zero policies on protecting student info from third parties. Big red flag in today’s world! 5. Budget Blues: $1M per year for devices (totaling $5M over 5 years) + $2.3M for infrastructure (accounting for e-rate reimbursement, but they haven’t even received the last one requested). Both estimates are lowballs, and they ignore costs for increased staffing, infrastructure upgrades, device losses, blue light glasses to protect students’ eyes, or extra tech support. What about the fiscal cliff? 6. Internet Upgrades Needed: Current network probably won’t cut it—upgrades are essential, but are they fully planned? Bottom line: The pitch was all about buying/deploying, ignoring academic pros/cons. The current proposal covers only middle and high schools (not elementary). Feels like “keeping up with other districts” vibes from 2 years ago. Aside from all this info… what is the reason we are even looking to do this? Are there lots of students that don’t have access to a laptop at home? Wouldn’t it be more economical to only supply those in need? There is no way that just because the personal model is said to cost less than the classroom, that it’s going to cost less in total in the long run. It’s just not possible. This absolutely sets students up for more screen time. Have you seen the negative impacts on that? Back to the question: What problem are we trying to solve? Let’s discuss real student and taxpayer impacts!

entities.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | I have heard some misconceptions from Thursday BOE Technology Update. We currently use a classroom approach to distribute chromebooks to high school and middle school students. This does require each classroom to have a higher number of chromebooks to match the hour with the largest class size. We are shifting to a personal chromebook model where each high school and middle school student will be assigned their own chromebook. Thursday’s Technology Update included these advantages to the change. 1- Money Savings - The personal chromebook model costs less than the classroom model. 2- Students can bring their personal chromebook home allowing for greater access to homework and Canva. 3- Students can more easily navigate the chromebook, as shared by Thursday’s student representative. This change in distribution does not mean students will be on technology more than before. It is simply a change in how chromebooks are assigned. This change provides greater efficiency for students and saves money for taxpayers. Win-Win. Transparency is only effective if it is connected to open, understandable communication. I hope this helps. Please feel free to ask questions. I’ll do my best to answer them. | kcdZzwZt.com

entities.text: WAKE UP, MISSOURI PARENTS! Our kids’ innocence is under attack in public schools. Schroer urges, this bill will “protect the innocence and integrity of children’s learning environment.” ￼ Contact your reps NOW—our taxpayer dollars shouldn’t fund this! #ProtectOurKids #SB483 #MissouriParentsUnite Click this link to see inside the book: https://simplebooklet.com/copyofv2meandearlandthed

entities.author: Kim Barkley
entities.text: For those that wish for clarity, these are the questions she’s probably asking herself: • Students can compare and contrast their own cultural background and beliefs with those of people with different worldviews. - who drives those conversations? How neutral is the person driving that conversation? How do we prevent partisanship? Our world is very divided. How do we ensure conversation around those worldviews is productive and not propagandizing. • The can demonstrate respect for different cultures by being open-minded, asking thoughtful questions, and challenging stereotypes. - Will someone try to compel “my” speech, i.e. pronoun usage. Is there going to be true clarity between culture vs ideology or could those lines get blurred?• Physical and emotional safety are foundational to creating an environment where everyone feels accepted, supported, and valued. - pointing to emotional safety here. In theory this is good, in practice, but does this come back to compelling speech or pushing an ideology?• School-acceptable behaviors may differ from those at home or in the community; one may need to adapt one's actions to different environments. - again, does this get blurry? Would you be required to use certain speech or accept changes to bathroom or locker room policies at school, and is it something you wouldn’t normally accept from a home standpoint. I believe the point she’s making is these guidelines are not clear enough and in today’s political climate, they could get blurry or abused.

entities.author: Erin GB
entities.text: Lauren Greenwood (owner of this page —School Watchlist)- if you’re running for school board, that role carries a HUGE responsibility to represent and protect all students — not just the ones who reflect your personal beliefs. Leadership in education requires open-mindedness, empathy, and the ability to prioritize student well-being above personal discomfort. Even if you don’t fully understand or agree with LGBTQ identities, the students who identify that way are still part of the community you would be elected to serve. These flags aren’t political statements — they’re signals of safety and as one poster stated earlier “nobody becomes LGBTQ for political purposes.”It saddens me to see you continue to create division by focusing on issues that stir people up. As someone seeking to serve on the school board, I hope you’ll prioritize the real challenges facing our district and work towards creating an environment of unity…… we are all on one team and all want the best for the students FHSD serves.

entities.author: School Watchlist
entities.text: When Inclusion Becomes a Source of Division You wanted proof here it is This flag was hung in multiple classrooms at Hollenbeck middle school This is a “Real photo”. Not Ai. The Question of Flags The paradox is simple. Inclusion for one group can be perceived as exclusion by another. This does not automatically invalidate the gesture. Public institutions may well have sound reasons for signalling support. But it challenges the idea that such acts are neutral or universally unifying. They are choices, and choices inevitably reflect priorities. Policy Violation • Policy 6242 Religious or Controversial Issues: https://go.boarddocs.com/mo/fhsdmo/Board.nsf/goto?open... Sign the petition: https://c.org/5wBwbGZ85c

entities.text: Hey Missouri families and educators! Lt. Gov. David Wasinger just launched the “Lieutenant Governor’s Award for American Patriotism” essay contest to celebrate America’s 250th anniversary and inspire patriotism in our kids. Open to all Missouri students in grades K-12. Write a letter using one of these prompts: • “I am proud to be an American because…” • “I love America because…” Word count limits: • Grades K-3: 50 words • Grades 4-6: 100 words • Grades 7-12: 200 words Submission deadline: Entries must be postmarked no later than March 1, 2026. Winners will be honored at a special ceremony and lunch at the Missouri State Capitol on June 26, 2026, where they’ll read their letters aloud! This is a great way for kids to reflect on our nation’s blessings of liberty, faith, family, and freedom. Get those entries in soon—spread the word! For full details: https://ltgov.mo.gov/lieutenant-governor-david-wasinger.../ Project requirements PDF: https://ltgov.mo.gov/.../Letters-to-Lt.-Governor-Project...

entities.author: School Watchlist
entities.text: WALKOUT HAPPENING NOW! Students at Francis Howell North are currently participating in a walkout right now. Reports say at least 50+ kids have left class to protest (details on the exact cause are still unclear—some are speculating it could be related to ICE/immigration enforcement, but it might not be. No official confirmation yet). This is happening DURING school hours, unlike Fort Zumwalt where similar things were organized AFTER school. Will these students be held responsible? Will there be absences marked, detentions, or other consequences like in past walkouts? Or will the district look the other way? Superintendent Mark Delaney hasn’t responded yet with any official statement (as far as I know), but this seems disruptive to the school day. Anyone have more details or eyewitness accounts? #FrancisHowellNorth #FHN #Walkout #StudentProtest

entities.text: Student Walk out UPDATE- Email from the district: let’s hope they follow their own rules February 12, 2026 FHN families: Some FHN students made the decision to leave their classes after 3rd period and walk out of the school building. FHN administrators are with the students and are directing students to move to a supervised location on campus. We are being told the walkout is a demonstration against recent actions by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). The District has provided guidance to all schools for navigating student protests. Our ultimate goal is to maintain a safe and secure school campus and to ensure that students do not present a major disruption to the learning environment. Here is some information about how we respond to student walkouts. We do not dismiss schools for walkouts, peaceful protests, or other demonstrations. Students who choose to participate in the walkout will be under adult supervision while on campus. Students will receive absence marks based on their actual attendance in each class, and they will face consequences for non-attendance or tardiness consistent with our normal procedures. Instruction will continue as scheduled. Students will not be given additional time to complete quizzes or exams that may be given during the walkout. Should a walkout happen during lunch, students who choose to participate will not be granted additional lunchtime. Consistent with MSHSAA bylaws and the FHSD Activities Handbook, students must attend school the entire day, or be marked excused by the principal, in order to participate in practices, rehearsals, or games for athletic teams or performance groups. Any verbal escalations, inappropriate behaviors, altercations, or other actions stemming from participation in the walkout will be subject to disciplinary action in accordance with the FHSD Code of Student Conduct. Students will be instructed to return to class as soon as the walkout concludes. Members of the media or general public wishing to observe or participate in the student-led walkout will not be permitted on campus during the instructional day. The principal has the authority to temporarily limit all traffic in and out, including parents and visitors, to protect student safety. Administrators and counselors will be available to assist students in processing their emotions. Every effort will be made to be consistent in our guidelines and consequences. The same policies and Code of Student Conduct that govern our work every day will also apply during any student walkouts. Thank you for helping us maintain safe learning environments for all students. FHN Admin Team

entities.author: Karen Sieve
entities.text: I question your motives, Lauren, and of anyone running for a seat on a public school board like Francis Howell when you ignore the fact PropRT (originally SB 3) will hurt St. Charles County public schools, libraries, fire departments, ambulance services, and the developmental disabilities board. Given inflation and continued growth of our county and local municipalities, drastic cuts will be necessary. It’s irresponsible for you to suggest that sales taxes will not increase in the future. The money has to come from somewhere. The Governor also has plans to cut income taxes, and last year, Missouri eliminated capital gains tax. The Governor is also using state funds for private education vouchers, which I assume you, Jane Puszkar, and David Jaworski support as well given your campaigns are funded by the St. Charles Republican Party. If PropRT is passed, sales taxes will increase, and if the Governor eliminates income tax, sales taxes will skyrocket and be regressive, meaning the elderly, the poor and middle class will bear the burden of the higher prices at the grocery store. Services like haircuts, lawn care, etc. will be taxed. What about prescription drugs?So maybe you should practice what you preach about transparency so the community knows that you really don’t support public schools. Vote NO on PropRT. Save our public schools.

The money has to come from somewhere. The Governor also has plans to cut income taxes, and last year, Missouri eliminated capital gains tax. The Governor is also using state funds for private education vouchers, which I assume you, Jane Puszkar, and David Jaworski support as well given your campaigns are funded by the St. Charles Republican Party. If PropRT is passed, sales taxes will increase, and if the Governor eliminates income tax, sales taxes will skyrocket and be regressive, meaning the elderly, the poor and middle class will bear the burden of the higher prices at the grocery store. Services like haircuts, lawn care, etc. will be taxed. What about prescription drugs?So maybe you should practice what you preach about transparency so the community knows that you really don’t support public schools. Vote NO on PropRT. Save our public schools.LikeReplyEdited1

entities.author: School Watchlist
entities.text: Francis Howell School District is failing to follow its own policies, putting ideology over rules and student well-being. Here’s the proof: 1. Human Sexuality Policy 6116 and Regulation explicitly state that staff should not make value judgments on sexuality, avoid conversations about it, and direct questions to parents. Yet, teachers are reading books about transgender surgeries to elementary kids and maintaining private “Pride libraries” in classrooms with books on boys having romantic encounters with boys—recommended as reading projects. This directly violates the policy. 2. Learning Commons Policy 6310 is ignored by allowing age-inappropriate books that clearly violate Missouri statutes (like those promoting explicit content) and the district’s own guidelines on educational suitability. 3. In-Classroom Library Policy (under 6310/6341) requires all books to be provided in a list to the board for review and prohibits bringing in books not already in the district library. This isn’t happening—unauthorized books are everywhere, the superintendent knows, and nothing’s being done. 4. Transgender Progress flags are hung in multiple classrooms violating Policy 6242 Religious or Controversial Issues. Parents, demand accountability! Contact the board and superintendent today at Board@fhsdschools.org. #FHSD #SchoolAccountability #ProtectOurKids Policy Links: • Human Sexuality Policy 6116: https://go.boarddocs.com/mo/fhsdmo/Board.nsf/goto?open... • Human Sexuality Regulation: https://go.boarddocs.com/.../Reg%206116%20-%20Human... • Learning Commons Policy 6310: https://go.boarddocs.com/.../P6310%20-%20Learning... • In-Classroom Library Policy (under 6310/6341): https://go.boarddocs.com/.../P6310%20-%20Learning... • Policy 6242 Religious or Controversial Issues: https://go.boarddocs.com/mo/fhsdmo/Board.nsf/goto?open...

entities.author: School Watchlist
entities.text: Attention Parents of Francis Howell North Students: Just a heads up (in case you missed it in ENews) – Sexual Abuse Prevention presentations from The Child Advocacy Center of Northeast Missouri are scheduled during English classes on the following dates: • February 3 • February 4 • February 5 • February 10 • February 11 • February 12 • April 13 • April 14 • April 15 • April 16 • April 17 I had the chance to review a private preview of the presentation materials beforehand, which informed my perspective. While I fully see the value in programs like this for educating on abuse prevention and empowering teens with knowledge about consent and boundaries, parts of it—like statements emphasizing that “every person has their own personal boundaries and consent,” and discussions that seem to normalize sexual relationships among teens—left me not 100% comfortable. It’s not about dismissing the program’s intent; it’s about highlighting that parents might want a say in how these sensitive topics are introduced, especially if it doesn’t align with their family values. I personally will be allowing my child to participate. For questions, concerns, or to get an opt-out form, please reach out to Dr. Erin Steep at erin.steep@fhsdschools.org or (636) 851-5031. Website: https://www.cacnemo.org/ Keeping you informed!

entities.text: Following district policy is not harassment. Raising concerns about age-appropriate content is not hate. Disagreeing does not justify abuse. What kind of learning community responds to concerns with intimidation and name-calling? Just a sample of threats and what I’ve been called during this process: • “Most recently, I was labeled a “faux (fake) Christian,” “white,” “heterosexual,” and warned “don’t screw up my kids’ diversity” • “They mess with one of our kids, they mess with all of us” • “Dimwitted” • “bully/intimidate/cause trouble” • “Toxic candidate” • “Book banning is for dummies” • “Anti-intellectual” • “Mouth breather” • “Idiot” • “Racist” • “Illiterate” • “Not competent to read” • “Children shouldn’t suffer for the sins of their parents” • “Stupid” • “People in green/wood houses shouldn't throw stones” • “living in glass houses, mind-bogglingly unaware of their own children's reality” This is deeply concerning, and it needs to be said. I have not attacked or harassed anyone. I have raised documented, firsthand concerns regarding my child’s 7th grade English class at Hollenbeck and both of my children’s school libraries. The irony is clear: this ‘learning community’—including the teacher herself—has exposed her identity far more than I ever did. Attacking my religion in response is inappropriate and reflects clear hypocrisy rather than engagement with the issue. This should concern every parent. Given this, I now question whether I should be the one issuing cease-and-desist letters sighting harassment, misrepresentations, extreme emotional distress, damage to my reputation. Would that take the focus off the kids? Because the focus hasn’t been on kids at all—it’s been on adult agendas/identities.

entities.text: WAS TRANSGENDER INSTRUCTION GIVEN TO VERY YOUNG STUDENTS WITHOUT PARENT CONSENT? Last night it was reported that a teacher allegedly has violated Board Policy 6116 (Human Sexuality) by discussing transgender-related topics with a very young audience. While board member Sarah Oelke quickly tries to dismiss in attempt to discredit THE TRUTH WILL COME OUT! Listen here: https://youtube.com/.../UgkxKJRO6uYAwk6si4g6v2IwL8hVQLh0B... This policy is explicit and unambiguous: Human sexuality instruction may not occur without prior parent notification and consent. That safeguard exists for a reason — to protect children and to respect parents. So the questions are simple and fair: • What are the ramifications for violating this policy? • How did this happen inside a classroom? • And most importantly — what concrete steps will the district take to ensure this never happens again? Parents should not have to discover policy violations after the fact, through their children. Transparency matters. Policies matter. And when they are broken, accountability must follow. Take Action: Email or call these decision-makers and demand they stop violating policy and protect our children: Chief Academic Officer Glenn Hancock – Glenn.Hancock@fhsdschools.org | (636) 851-4036 Superintendent Mark Delaney – mark.delaney@fhsdschools.org | (636) 851-4000 t

entities.text: SCHOOL CHOICE good or bad? Governor Mike Kehoe says..“Again, open enrollment is not about weakening public education,” said Kehoe. “It’s about strengthening it because when families have choices, schools are pushed to innovate. They’re pushed to improve and respond to the needs of the students they serve.” Rep. Kem Smith, D-Florissant, a longtime teacher, said open enrollment would not improve school quality. “Open enrollment creates winners and losers,” she said. “I know that this body is looking for a way to improve education, to hold schools more accountable. Why This Book Violates District Policy • District policy prohibits: • Explicit sexual descriptions, including child molestation, rape, and references to bestiality • Sexual nudity • Violence, including sexual assault and child abuse • Materials glamorizing or instructing drug/alcohol use, as the book contains drug abuse references • References to animal cruelty • Excessive or unnecessary profanity, even if mild/infrequent Parents: Bestseller status or awards do NOT make this book appropriate for minors. A Stolen Life contains explicit sexual descriptions of rape and child molestation, drug abuse references, and traumatic violence. These elements directly conflict with district policy for school library materials. Do you think this belongs in our school libraries? Comment below and share this post to raise awareness! entities.text: Public record shows the superintendent hire passed 6–1, with Jane Puszkar as the only NO vote. That hire later cost taxpayers ~$230,000, and he never worked a single day. Oversight only works when a majority is willing to act. That’s why I’m supporting Puszkar, Greenwood, and Jaworski on April 7. This post reflects my personal views and is based on publicly available information.

entities.text: Book Challenge Alert: Kingdom of the Wicked by Kerri Maniscalco Locations: Francis Howell Central | Francis Howell North Interest Level: Adult Rating: 5 (Extreme language and/or violence) Contains: • Occult and witchcraft themes (spells, rituals, demon summoning) • Demonic and supernatural elements (portrayal of demons as characters) • Violence and murder (graphic descriptions of killings and revenge) • Dark moral undertones (vengeance, manipulation, morally gray choices) • Romantic content • Spiritual conflict (themes that may contradict traditional faith values) Why This Book Violates District Policy • District policy prohibits: • Graphic/Criminal Violence • The story features a brutal murder and criminal acts consistent with “purposeful conduct that injures another’s body”. Martin Locations: Francis Howell High School | Francis Howell North Interest Level: Adult Rating: 5 (Extreme language and/or violence) Contains: - Graphic sexual content (including incest, rape) - Extreme violence & child abuse - Profanity Why This Book Violates District Policy District policy prohibits: Explicit sexual descriptions (including masturbation, vaginal sex, oral sex, anal sex, oral-anal sex, use of sex toys, ejaculation, sadomasochistic abuse) Materials glamorizing or instructing drug/alcohol use Excessive or unnecessary profanity Violence such as rape, sexual assault, child abuse This book contains these elements, making it in direct conflict with Board-approved collection standards. Parents: Bestseller status or awards do NOT make this book appropriate for minors. Literary acclaim doesn’t erase explicit sexual content, drug glamorization, and extreme violence. entities.text: How Parents Can Check Their Child’s School Library (FHSD) Step 1: Go to the online library https://fhsdschools.follettdestiny.com/portal/portal... • Once on the catalog screen, change Location to “Francis Howell Schools” to search the entire district (Ref: Screenshot 1) ⸻ Step 2: Search • Use Keyword (recommended) • This allows you to search by topics or themes, even if you don’t know a specific title or author ⸻ Step 3: Review results • Look for “Interest Level” (ex: Elementary, Middle, Young Adult) • This can help you question whether the content fits your child’s age (Ref: Screenshot 2) ⸻ Step 4: Click “Details” • Read the summary/description of the book (Ref: Screenshot 3) ⸻ Step 5: Click “Copies” (top right) • See which schools currently have the book (Ref: Screenshot 4) ⸻ How to Challenge a Book • First, contact your child’s building principal • If needed, complete the district’s official review form and submit it as instructed Book Challenge Form https://resources.finalsite.net/.../Review-of-Learning... entities.text: It’s CENSORSHIP. Voters should be paying attention. Instead of removing the inappropriate material, they’re now trying to rewrite policy to silence the only board member fighting for our kids innocence—effectively stripping a duly elected board member of her First Amendment rights. Let that sink in. Sexually explicit and wildly age-inappropriate books continue to be allowed in Francis Howell Schools (elementary included!). When school board member Jane Puszkar tries to shine a light on this—by reading the actual content aloud at board meetings and speaking out on conservative talk radio—the response from the mostly liberal board isn’t accountability. Rather than protect children or respect parents, the Francis Howell School Board is willing to go to unbelievable depths to cover their shame and suppress the truth. This isn’t about politics anymore. It’s about free speech, transparency, and protecting kids. Parents should be outraged. Voters should be paying attention.

entities.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | California teachers can no longer hide children’s gender identities from their parents following a permanent injunction issued Monday in a class action lawsuit. The lawsuit was filed by teachers who felt a moral duty to protect children and strongly objected to being dishonest with parents about their kids, as the state’s “Parental Exclusion Policies” required them to do. Several California Department of Education policies were “designed to create a zone of secrecy around a school student who expresses gender incongruity,” according to the court order, preventing teachers and school staff from sharing vital information with parents. “Today’s incredible victory finally, and permanently, ends California’s dangerous and unconstitutional regime of gender secrecy policies in schools,” Paul M. Jonna, special counsel at Thomas More Society, which represented the teachers and parents in the lawsuit, said in a statement following the decision. “The Court’s comprehensive ruling -- granting summary judgment on all claims -- protects all California parents, students, and teachers, and it restores sanity and common sense. With this decisive ruling from Judge Benitez, all state and local school officials that mandate gender secrecy policies should cease all enforcement or face severe legal consequences.” The case explored four questions: * Whether the Fourteenth Amendment’s substantive due process clause provides parents a right to access information about their child’s gender identity * Whether the First Amendment’s free exercise of religion clause does the same * Whether the First Amendment provides religious teachers “a right to provide gender information to parents” based on free exercise protections * Whether the First Amendment provides public school teachers “a right to communicate accurate gender information to parents” based on free speech protections “In each case, this Court concludes that, as a matter of law, the answer is ‘yes,’” Bush-appointed U.S. District Court Judge Roger Benitez wrote in his 52-page opinion. “Parents have a right to receive gender information and teachers have a right to provide to parents accurate information about a child’s gender identity.” Under Democratic Gov. Gavin Newsom, California in 2024 became the first state to bar schools from requiring staff to notify parents if a child requests a name or pronoun change, seeks access to opposite-sex facilities, or attempts to join opposite-sex sports teams. State education code permits athletes to participate on whichever team is “consistent with his or her gender identity,” and California’s Civil Rights Act further includes “gender identity” under its definition of sex. “Parental involvement [is] essential to the healthy maturation of schoolchildren,” the court opinion said. “California’s public school system parental exclusion policies place a communication barrier between parents and teachers.” “Although as stated previously, the State’s desire to protect vulnerable children from harassment and discrimination is laudable, the parental exclusion policies create a trifecta of harm: they harm the child who needs parental guidance and possibly mental health intervention to determine if the incongruence is organic or whether it is the result of bullying, peer pressure, or a fleeting impulse,” the order continued. “They harm the parents by depriving them of the long-recognized Fourteenth Amendment right to care, guide, and make health care decisions for their children, and by substantially burdening many parents’ First Amendment right to train their children in their sincerely held religious beliefs. And finally, they harm teachers who are compelled to violate the sincerely held beliefs and the parent’s rights by forcing them to conceal information they feel is critical for the welfare of their students.” All content created by the Daily Caller News Foundation, an independent and nonpartisan newswire service, is available without charge to any legitimate news publisher that can provide a large audience. entities.text: STEVEN BLAIR’S BOARD MEETING REMARKS UNDER SCRUTINY Violation of Francis Howell School District policy during an official public board meeting — or just another “green thing”? Either way, it doesn’t sit right. During a public, taxpayer-funded board meeting, School Board President Steven Blair told the public how we should vote on Senate Bill 3, urging opposition so the district can continue overspending. FHSD policy and Missouri law are clear: District platforms may explain the impact of legislation — but they may NOT advocate for or against a ballot measure. Explaining legislation = appropriate Telling taxpayers how to vote = not appropriate Listen for yourself: https://www.youtube.com/live/5JDMgoCLcic... It appears the district intends to charge ahead with reckless spending, including: • $78,000,000 over budget on the new high school • $230,000 paid to a superintendent who never started • …and plenty more under review More ongoing spending projects are now under scrutiny — stay tuned. I’m voting YES on Senate Bill 3 this April. Anyone else keeping tabs?

entities.author: School Watchlist
entities.text: THIS IS ACUAL DISCRIMINATION It’s interesting how often people say they’re “not against anybody’s religion,” yet in the same breath argue that anyone with a biblical worldview shouldn’t have a voice in public education. Here’s the problem with that thinking: Public schools are meant to serve everyone — including families who hold religious beliefs. Wanting people of faith excluded from decision-making doesn’t promote neutrality; it promotes one worldview while shutting out another. You don’t have to agree with someone’s beliefs to respect their right to participate. A biblical foundation shapes many people’s morals, ethics, and approach to leadership — the same way others draw from philosophy, culture, or personal life experience. Singling out Christians as uniquely unfit to serve isn’t separation of church and state… it’s discrimination.
