entities.text: The TRUTH is we’re protecting their innocence. There is NO SHAME in that. SET BOUNDARIES with your child’s SCHOOL!
entities.rawObservedText: The TRUTH is we’re protecting their innocence. There is NO SHAME in that. SET BOUNDARIES with your child’s SCHOOL!
entities.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | Normalize keeping your children away from children who are too exposed Normalize keeping your kids away from children who are too exposed. In today’s world, there are kids with full access to the internet, social media, mature shows, and things their little minds shouldn’t have to process yet. And honestly… it shows. My boys are 6, 5, and 3, and sometimes my husband and I wonder if we’re sheltering them. But the truth is, we’re protecting their innocence. We don’t want them learning things that are far too heavy and too mature for their developing brains. Normalize saying no. Normalize not letting your young children be alone with other children, even “good kids,” simply because you don’t know what those kids have seen, heard, or experienced. This isn’t about judgment, it’s about safety. I was a child who was exposed to way too much, way too young. And I can say, it stays with you. It shapes you. It affects you in ways you don’t even recognize until much later. So if you’re the parent who chooses to limit access, supervise closely, set boundaries, and protect your child’s childhood..you’re not overreacting. You’re not controlling. You’re being a present, aware, loving parent. Protecting their innocence isn’t sheltering. It’s parenting. | n51evETkPd.com

entities.attachmentSummary: Amy Gryder’s latest video is worth a watch — for all the wrong reasons. Right out of the gate, she downplays concerns about bathrooms and locker rooms. She calls girls “cisgen kids” and acts like it’s no big deal if biological males are changing next to them. That’s the mindset we’re dealing with. Then she dodges the sports issue — but doesn’t mention SHE FILED an official opposition in Jefferson City in SUPPORT OF ALLOWING BOYS IN GIRLS' SPORTS. If she gets her way, your local school board will decide. And she wants a seat. That’s not leadership. That’s an agenda. And it’s unfair to our daughters. If Amy Gryder and Sarah Oelke win, they’ll team up with far-left board members Carolie Owens and Steven Blair. And yes — your daughters will be changing next to boys and competing against them. It’s that simple. | 9siR4kTlnOTIkMGWbSSSteq7ofEgPmRSrKMqfluvl9s | WF6EpFjKVK.com

entities.text: TOMORROW ON AIR! When: Tomorrow at 7:00 a.m. Where: KFTK‑FM “97.1 FM Talk” in the St. Louis area. Attention parents, community members, and supporters of our kids at the Francis Howell School District: I’m honored to join school board member Jane Puszkar tomorrow morning on the The Marc Cox Morning Show to speak out against explicit books in our school libraries. We believe our children deserve safe, age-appropriate learning environments, and we’ll be discussing why explicit content in school libraries is a serious concern, what many parents are seeing, and how we can work together for strong standards. I hope you’ll tune in, spread the word, and stand with us in protecting what our kids read and learn in our schools. Thank you for your support! — Concerned parent, Lauren Greenwood

entities.text: Parents, You Need to Hear This! Francis Howell School District parents Jane Puszkarr and Lauren Greenwood joined The Vic Porcelli Show (NewsTalk STL 101.9 / 94.1 FM) to sound the alarm about inappropriate, sexually explicit books being made available to students in our schools. entities.text: Big win today — another parent has stepped up and contacted Congressman Bob Onder’s office. His team responded and agreed to escalate the issue, bringing much-needed visibility and light to what’s happening in the Francis Howell School District. Who is Bob Onder? Bob Onder is now the U.S. Representative for Missouri’s 3rd Congressional District (as of January 2025). He has positioned himself as a leading voice defending parental rights, opposing what he calls the “radical gender ideology,” and working to block gender interventions on children. ⸻ What you can do right now: 1. Speak out — submit public comments to your school board and local leaders. board@fhsdschools.org 2. Contact Congressman Onder’s office — ask him to continue pushing for protection of children and to bring pressure to bear on FHSD. Justin.Camp@mail.house.gov 3. Share this post — let more parents and voices step in. 4. Attend school board meetings — demand transparency, accountability, and parental control of curriculum. We are shining a light. We are making them hear us. Let’s do this together.

entities.text: Warning Non-binary pronouns being taught in Spanish class (FHSD North HS) Non-binary pronouns are absolutely tied to gender identity — that’s not even up for debate. Non-binary pronouns (they/them, ze/zir, xe/xem, etc.) are directly connected to gender identity. Gender identity is how a person understands and experiences their own gender (male, female, both, neither, or somewhere in between). Pronouns are a way language reflects and respects that identity in everyday communication. So when you are teaching students non-binary pronouns, you are, in fact, teaching about gender identity. That is precisely what our policy prohibits. Send concerns to Superintendent mark.delaney@fhsdschools.org and Helene.Herauf@ed.gov to update the open Dept of Education Complaint OCR 07251345

events.author: School Watchlist
events.text: It’s CENSORSHIP. Voters should be paying attention. Instead of removing the inappropriate material, they’re now trying to rewrite policy to silence the only board member fighting for our kids innocence—effectively stripping a duly elected board member of her First Amendment rights. Let that sink in. Sexually explicit and wildly age-inappropriate books continue to be allowed in Francis Howell Schools (elementary included!). When school board member Jane Puszkar tries to shine a light on this—by reading the actual content aloud at board meetings and speaking out on conservative talk radio—the response from the mostly liberal board isn’t accountability. Rather than protect children or respect parents, the Francis Howell School Board is willing to go to unbelievable depths to cover their shame and suppress the truth. This isn’t about politics anymore. It’s about free speech, transparency, and protecting kids. Parents should be outraged. Voters should be paying attention.

events.author: School Watchlist
events.text: Proud to support a school board candidate who will fight to protect our children’s innocence and defend the rights of parents. Our kids deserve safe schools, age-appropriate content, and leaders who value clear, objective policy — where words mean what they say and rules aren’t left up to personal interpretation. This election matters.

events.text: STEVEN BLAIR’S BOARD MEETING REMARKS UNDER SCRUTINY Violation of Francis Howell School District policy during an official public board meeting — or just another “green thing”? Either way, it doesn’t sit right. During a public, taxpayer-funded board meeting, School Board President Steven Blair told the public how we should vote on Senate Bill 3, urging opposition so the district can continue overspending. FHSD policy and Missouri law are clear: District platforms may explain the impact of legislation — but they may NOT advocate for or against a ballot measure. Explaining legislation = appropriate Telling taxpayers how to vote = not appropriate Listen for yourself: https://www.youtube.com/live/5JDMgoCLcic... It appears the district intends to charge ahead with reckless spending, including: • $78,000,000 over budget on the new high school • $230,000 paid to a superintendent who never started • …and plenty more under review More ongoing spending projects are now under scrutiny — stay tuned. I’m voting YES on Senate Bill 3 this April. Anyone else keeping tabs?

events.author: Bryce Krawzik
events.text: Matt Stolle, your argument relies on a fundamental mischaracterization of what school libraries actually provide. Equating books that feature LGBTQ+ characters or themes with explicit adult content is a common but incorrect talking point. Having a diverse identity is not inherently adult or sexual, and these books are selected by certified professionals to be age appropriate for the students they serve. Furthermore, the term grooming has a very specific and serious definition involving predatory behavior. Using it to describe educators providing inclusive literature is both factually wrong and deeply harmful to the actual safety of children.The job of a school is indeed to teach kids to read, write, and think critically. You cannot think critically if you are shielded from the reality that diverse people exist in the world. As a student in this district, I see that these books are not about bypassing parents. They are about ensuring that every student, including those from LGBTQ+ families or those who are LGBTQ+ themselves, feels seen and safe in their learning environment. Education should be about expanding a student’s horizons and fostering empathy, which are skills that help us navigate a world full of different perspectives.It is also important to remember that this is a public school district funded by and for the entire community. Public institutions have a duty to represent all citizens, not just those who hold one specific set of beliefs. While parents have every right to guide their own children's reading choices, they do not have the right to dictate what is available to other people's children or to erase the representation of entire groups of people from a public space. If a family requires an educational environment that aligns strictly and exclusively with their personal private or religious views, that is what private education is designed for. Public education, by definition, must remain a space that reflects the full human experience and respects the rights of every student to feel included.

events.author: Bryce Krawzik
events.text: Carrie Johnson dismissing the lived experiences of students with a single word doesn’t change the overwhelming consensus from the American Psychological Association and the American Academy of Pediatrics, both of which recognize that children can and do identify as part of the LGBTQ+ community from a young age. Claiming that representation is wrong ignores the clinical reality that access to age appropriate, inclusive literature is a vital protective factor against the high rates of depression, anxiety, and suicidal ideation that marginalized youth face when they are isolated. These books are not about adult themes but are curated tools that provide children with the language to understand their own emotions and foster empathy for their peers, which is a foundational goal of any public education system. Furthermore, public school libraries are legally and ethically obligated to serve the entire student body, not just the viewpoints of one specific group. Denying the existence of these children or removing their access to information does not stop them from being LGBTQ+, it only ensures they feel unsafe and unsupported in their own community. True education is about preparing all children to navigate a diverse world with kindness and factual understanding rather than fear and exclusion.

events.author: Bryce Krawzik
events.text: Jane Puszkar, I strongly encourage you to look beyond your personal perspective and examine the actual consensus within the fields of adolescent psychology, medical science, and constitutional law. By labeling inclusive literature as an agenda or pornography, you are fundamentally mischaracterizing age appropriate educational resources that serve as a critical lifeline for students. To be clear, these books are curated by professionals to reflect diverse identities rather than to provide graphic content. Equating the existence of LGBTQ+ people to pornography is a harmful falsehood that ignores the reality of human identity and creates a dangerous environment for marginalized students. For a child experiencing gender dysphoria, access to this literature is a vital mental health resource that provides the language needed to understand their emotions, which is essential for healthy self regulation and development. According to the American Psychological Association and the American Academy of Pediatrics, the lack of representation and social support in schools is a direct contributor to the alarmingly high rates of depression, anxiety, and self harm among LGBTQ+ youth. Providing these books is quite literally a matter of suicide prevention and overall student safety. Furthermore, restricting access to information in public institutions often borders on a violation of First Amendment rights and ignores the fact that public school libraries must serve the entire community rather than just one specific viewpoint. These stories also benefit cisgender and straight students by fostering empathy and teaching them how to coexist in a diverse society, which is a necessary skill for the modern workforce. When you deny children the ability to see themselves or their peers reflected in their education, you are not protecting them from an imaginary threat. Instead, you are isolating vulnerable kids and creating a culture of shame that leads to long term psychological trauma. Understanding the truth requires looking at the human impact of these policies and recognizing that every child, regardless of their background or identity, deserves to feel seen, safe, and supported in their learning environment.

events.author: Bryce Krawzik
events.text: Matt Stolle, parental involvement is a vital part of education, and every parent absolutely has the right to guide their own child’s reading choices. However, there is a significant legal and ethical difference between a parent's right to guide their own child and an attempt to restrict access for the entire student body.In fact, the Francis Howell School District already has policies in place (such as the Library Opt-Out form) that allow parents to specifically restrict their own children from checking out certain materials or genres. This ensures that you have the "consent" and control you are asking for regarding your own family's boundaries.In a public district, the standard is to provide a broad range of professionally curated materials and then allow individual families to decide what is right for them. When one group of parents demands the removal of books entirely, they are effectively overriding the parental consent of other families who want their children to have access to those stories. By removing these books, the district isn't protecting parents; it is removing the choice from all parents. Public education is built on the idea that we can coexist with different values, and that requires keeping the library a space for everyone rather than a space limited by the preferences of a few.

events.author: School Watchlist
events.text: Warning Non-binary pronouns being taught in Spanish class (FHSD North HS) Non-binary pronouns are absolutely tied to gender identity — that’s not even up for debate. Non-binary pronouns (they/them, ze/zir, xe/xem, etc.) are directly connected to gender identity. Gender identity is how a person understands and experiences their own gender (male, female, both, neither, or somewhere in between). Pronouns are a way language reflects and respects that identity in everyday communication. So when you are teaching students non-binary pronouns, you are, in fact, teaching about gender identity. That is precisely what our policy prohibits. Send concerns to Superintendent mark.delaney@fhsdschools.org and Helene.Herauf@ed.gov to update the open Dept of Education Complaint OCR 07251345

events.text: Taxpayers, the Missouri State Auditor’s report on the Francis Howell School District’s superintendent hiring debacle with Dr. Mike Dominguez exposes wasted money and weak leadership. The district paid a search firm over $40,000 — yet we’ve never been refunded despite the $229k+ payout to a superintendent who never started. Some have said Board President Steven Blair was tasked with pursuing that refund. He allegedly heard “no,” tucked his tail, and backed down. Why does Steven Blair run to the lawyers for every move? Our legal expenses have more than doubled since FY 2022: • 2022: $96,627 • 2023: $107,880 • 2024: $134,130 • 2025: $216,980 • 2026: $144,116 YTD At this rate, 2026 could be our highest year yet — all on your tax dollars. Action step: Email Board President Steven Blair at steven.blair@fhsdschools.org and ask him why he didn’t fight harder for your tax dollars and why legal fees keep skyrocketing. Is this the passive leadership we want protecting our wallets? Real accountability means demanding better — not rolling over. Parents deserve board members who fight for fiscal responsibility. What do you think? #FHSD #TaxpayerAccountability #stevenblair #carolieowens #FHSD

events.text: TRANSPARENCY ISN’T HARASSMENT. PARENTAL INVOLVEMENT ISN’T EXTREMISM. If you classify bringing the TRUTH about what’s actually happening in your child’s classroom as “harassment,” then you’ve got a serious misconception about what harassment actually is. Sharing proof, of what’s being recommended or provided isn’t bullying — it’s called being an involved parent. It’s called transparency. It’s called PROTECTING KIDS and YOUR PARENTAL RIGHTS. Real harassment is trying to silence parents who dare to look inside the classroom and speak up about what they find. Real harassment is treating moms and dads like enemies for simply letting other parents know what their children are being taught and influenced. If we can’t agree on that basic principle, we’ve lost our way. What do you think — is speaking truth in your child’s education protected, or is it being twisted into something it’s not? Drop your thoughts below. #ParentalRights #EducationTransparency #KnowWhatsInTheClassroom #FHSD #FrancisHowell

events.text: SCHOOL FUNDING REALITY CHECK: STOP THE ENDLESS MONEY REQUESTS - THE DATA DOESN’T LIE — WHY IS IT NEVER ENOUGH? Hey School Board — what’s your story this time? Blaming the state doesn’t work when the data shows revenue is UP $7.1M this year and $17M over five years. Try again. At last night’s FHSD Board meeting, Carl Suri (the man in the orange shirt) delivered one of the clearest, most data-driven explanations I’ve heard about school funding. He didn’t get emotional. He just walked through the actual numbers: • District revenue is now $245 million — up $7.1 million this year alone • That increase came entirely from the state (up 10.75%) • Over the last five years, state revenue is up $17 million — a 32% increase • Per-student state funding is at an all-time high, even after inflation His point was simple and hard to argue with: the money keeps going up, yet the district still acts like it’s never enough. He questioned why we keep hearing calls for more local taxes or fund transfers when the data shows revenue has been rising steadily. If you’ve ever felt like “just a little more money” is a permanent answer instead of a temporary one, watch this segment. It’s calm, factual, and cuts through the usual talking points. Link starts right at his comments: https://www.youtube.com/live/SwzYuBTzlnQ?t=218 Watch it. Share it. The numbers matter.

Parents aren’t harassers for asking hard questions and protecting their kids. The double standard is clear: data and parental rights matter. Watch the full meeting and decide for yourselves. events.text: PARENTS THE LONGER YOU WAIT and you don't hold your child's schools accountable gives these guys more time to dictate what's best for your child's physical mental and emotional health. Don’t be afraid to speak out for your kids because they are voiceless and rely on you. Parents — Know Your Rights You do not have to accept every lesson, survey, or program the school offers. Opt out of surveys and questionnaires. Many are designed to collect personal information about your child’s beliefs, mental health, family life, or identity. You can refuse participation. Request to preview all surveys, social-emotional lessons, and sensitive materials before they are given to your child. Put everything in writing. Send a clear opt-out notice and keep a copy for your records. Stay informed and connected. Talk with other parents, attend school board meetings, and share information. Your child’s education and values start at home. You have the right — and the responsibility — to protect both.

events.beforeText: Student Walk out UPDATE- Email from the district: let’s hope they follow their own rules February 12, 2026 FHN families: Some FHN students made the decision to leave their classes after 3rd period and walk out of the school building. FHN administrators are with the students and are directing students to move to a supervised location on campus. We are being told the walkout is a demonstration against recent actions by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). The District has provided guidance to all schools for navigating student protests. Our ultimate goal is to maintain a safe and secure school campus and to ensure that students do not present a major disruption to the learning environment. Here is some information about how we respond to student walkouts. We do not dismiss schools for walkouts, peaceful protests, or other demonstrations. Students who choose to participate in the walkout will be under adult supervision while on campus. Students will receive absence marks based on their actual attendance in each class, and they will face consequences for non-attendance or tardiness consistent with our normal procedures. Instruction will continue as scheduled. Students will not be given additional time to complete quizzes or exams that may be given during the walkout. Should a walkout happen during lunch, students who choose to participate will not be granted additional lunchtime. Consistent with MSHSAA bylaws and the FHSD Activities Handbook, students must attend school the entire day, or be marked excused by the principal, in order to participate in practices, rehearsals, or games for athletic teams or performance groups. Any verbal escalations, inappropriate behaviors, altercations, or other actions stemming from participation in the walkout will be subject to disciplinary action in accordance with the FHSD Code of Student Conduct. Students will be instructed to return to class as soon as the walkout concludes. Members of the media or general public wishing to observe or participate in the student-led walkout will not be permitted on campus during the instructional day. The principal has the authority to temporarily limit all traffic in and out, including parents and visitors, to protect student safety. Administrators and counselors will be available to assist students in processing their emotions. Every effort will be made to be consistent in our guidelines and consequences. The same policies and Code of Student Conduct that govern our work every day will also apply during any student walkouts. Thank you for helping us maintain safe learning environments for all students. FHN Admin Team

events.text: Warning Non-binary pronouns being taught in Spanish class (FHSD North HS) Non-binary pronouns are absolutely tied to gender identity — that’s not even up for debate. Non-binary pronouns (they/them, ze/zir, xe/xem, etc.) are directly connected to gender identity. Gender identity is how a person understands and experiences their own gender (male, female, both, neither, or somewhere in between). Pronouns are a way language reflects and respects that identity in everyday communication. So when you are teaching students non-binary pronouns, you are, in fact, teaching about gender identity. That is precisely what our policy prohibits. Send concerns to Superintendent mark.delaney@fhsdschools.org and Helene.Herauf@ed.gov to update the open Dept of Education Complaint OCR 07251345

events.text: Wentzville School District Settles Transgender Bathroom Lawsuit with Missouri AG Great news for transparency and parental rights in Wentzville R-IV Schools! The district has reached a settlement with Attorney General Catherine Hanaway, resolving a 2023 Sunshine Law case. The board was accused of discussing a transgender student bathroom and locker room access policy in closed sessions (June 2023) instead of openly with the public. Key points of the April 2026 agreement: • No admission of wrongdoing by the district • Acknowledges parents’ fundamental right to know about and participate in decisions affecting their children’s education, safety, and welfare • Commits to full compliance with Missouri’s Open Meetings/Sunshine Law • Requires Sunshine Law training for board members and staff • Must post a public statement about the case and settlement on the district website This reinforces that important school policies should be debated in the open, not behind closed doors. Full settlement: https://ago.mo.gov/.../State-v.-Wentzville-Settlement... What do you think—transparency wins? Share your thoughts!

events.text: Student Walk out UPDATE- Email from the district: let’s hope they follow their own rules February 12, 2026 FHN families: Some FHN students made the decision to leave their classes after 3rd period and walk out of the school building. FHN administrators are with the students and are directing students to move to a supervised location on campus. We are being told the walkout is a demonstration against recent actions by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). The District has provided guidance to all schools for navigating student protests. Our ultimate goal is to maintain a safe and secure school campus and to ensure that students do not present a major disruption to the learning environment. Here is some information about how we respond to student walkouts. We do not dismiss schools for walkouts, peaceful protests, or other demonstrations. Students who choose to participate in the walkout will be under adult supervision while on campus. Students will receive absence marks based on their actual attendance in each class, and they will face consequences for non-attendance or tardiness consistent with our normal procedures. Instruction will continue as scheduled. Students will not be given additional time to complete quizzes or exams that may be given during the walkout. Should a walkout happen during lunch, students who choose to participate will not be granted additional lunchtime. Consistent with MSHSAA bylaws and the FHSD Activities Handbook, students must attend school the entire day, or be marked excused by the principal, in order to participate in practices, rehearsals, or games for athletic teams or performance groups. Any verbal escalations, inappropriate behaviors, altercations, or other actions stemming from participation in the walkout will be subject to disciplinary action in accordance with the FHSD Code of Student Conduct. Students will be instructed to return to class as soon as the walkout concludes. Members of the media or general public wishing to observe or participate in the student-led walkout will not be permitted on campus during the instructional day. The principal has the authority to temporarily limit all traffic in and out, including parents and visitors, to protect student safety. Administrators and counselors will be available to assist students in processing their emotions. Every effort will be made to be consistent in our guidelines and consequences. The same policies and Code of Student Conduct that govern our work every day will also apply during any student walkouts. Thank you for helping us maintain safe learning environments for all students. FHN Admin Team

events.text: I looked into the board conduct issue, and the claim here seems overstated. FHSD does have board-conduct and ethics policies, but the available policy language is about board members acting professionally, not acting individually on behalf of the Board, and understanding that authority rests with the Board as a body in a legal session. I have not seen a policy that says wearing a board name tag at a public community event automatically equals district endorsement.At most, someone could ask whether the name tag created confusion about whether she was there personally or officially. That is a fair question. But jumping from that to “formal review and dismissal” is a huge leap unless someone can cite the exact FHSD policy and the exact legal removal process. An elected board member attending a public, family-friendly community event is not the same thing as the district formally endorsing that event.

events.author: Kaylee Morris
events.text: Jane Puszkar I never screamed or mentioned the separation of church and state. I simply asked School Watchlist a question, but since you brought that up yourself, I’ll inform you more accurately.First, your claim that “the country was founded on Christian values” is not supported by historical records. The Founders came from diverse Christian denominations, but they explicitly rejected the idea of a government tied to any religion. After independence, there was widespread agreement that the new nation must not have an official religion, and that government must not endorse or support any church.Source: https://www.loc.gov/exhibits/religion/rel06.htmlSecond, the idea that “separation of church and state was meant to keep government out of religion, not religion out of government” is also incorrect. Thomas Jefferson, the very person who coined the phrase, stated clearly in his 1802 letter to the Danbury Baptists that the First Amendment builds “a wall of separation between Church and State.” That wall protects both directions, government cannot interfere with religion, and religion cannot wield government power or receive government endorsement.Source: https://founders.archives.gov/documents/Jefferson/01-36-02-0056Roger Williams, founder of Rhode Island, also argued that government involvement corrupts religion and that a “hedge or wall of separation” is necessary to keep the church pure and independent.Source: https://americanheritage.org/roger-williams-first-call-for-separation-of-church-and-state-in-america/Third, your suggestion that religion was intended to be part of government contradicts the Constitution itself. Article VI explicitly prohibits any religious test for public office, ensuring that government positions are open to people of all faiths or none. This was a deliberate rejection of the idea that the United States government should be Christian or tied to Christianity.Source: https://constitution.congress.gov/constitution/article-6/Finally, the Establishment Clause, mostly written by James Madison, was created because the Founders had seen firsthand the harm caused when governments endorse or enforce religion. They agreed that the federal government must stay neutral toward religion, and by 1833 every state had disestablished its official church.Source: https://constitutioncenter.org/the-constitution/amendments/amendment-i/interpretations/264So no, the Founders did not intend religion to guide government, nor did they believe the United States was founded on Christian values in any governmental sense. They intentionally built a system where religion is personal, not governmental, and where public officials must not use their government roles to promote their personal faith.If you are going to talk about the separation of church and state, you should at least talk about it accurately. These are literal words straight from our Founders and the Constitution. Please educate yourself

events.author: Amy Mallams
events.text: Transgender People Are NOT a Threat to Public SafetyAnti-trans rhetoric portrays transgender people as violent, predatory, and/or hypersexual. In reality, transgender people are far more likely to experience harassment and violence than to inflict harm on others. Myths about transgender people often fall into two main categories: 1.) claims that transgender people are inherently violent 2.) claims that transgender people are sexual predators. NEITHER of these claims is supported by evidence. Instead, such false narratives distort public perception and fuel policies that put transgender communities in danger. These false narratives are not just misunderstandings; they are part of what scholars call a moral panic. Moral panic is when fear is exaggerated and directed at a marginalized group, painting them as a threat to society. Moral panics recycle old stigmas and anxieties (usually about race, gender, or sexuality) to justify discrimination and criminalization.Scholars note that moral panics often emerge as a response to social change; a way for communities to make sense of changing norms or perceived threats to traditional values. Throughout U.S. history, “protect the children” rhetoric has been used to vilify different groups: casting Black men as threats to white women,branding gay men as predators, and nowportraying transgender people as dangerous in schools and public bathrooms. These myths follow the same pattern, weaponizing fear to roll back civil rights under the guise of safety.Are transgender people a threat to public safety?NO. There is NO evidence that transgender people are more likely to engage in violent or criminal behavior than cisgender people. Research conducted on criminology and public safety consistently shows that gender identity does NOT predict criminal behavior. Studies find NO evidence that transgender people commit crimes at higher rates than cisgender people; instead, transgender people are more likely to experience discrimination and over-policing, facing disproportionate surveillance and punishment by law enforcement even when NO offense has been committed.According to the Bureau of Justice Statistics, transgender people were four times more likely to be victimized by violent crimes than cisgender people. Studies also document that transgender individuals experience disproportionately high rates of harassment, intimate violence, and hate crimes compared to cisgender people.These patterns show that transgender communities are far more vulnerable to violence, NOT more likely to commit it.These findings extend to public spaces, especially bathrooms. Studies consistently find that gender-inclusive restrooms and nondiscrimination policies do NOT compromise safety. In fact, places that have passed inclusive bathroom laws remain just as safe as they were before and had NO rise in crime or misconduct. Conversely, evidence shows that transgender people are at greater risk in bathrooms and other public facilities. Research from numerous medical, legal, and policy organizations consistently finds that gender-inclusive restrooms and nondiscrimination policies do NOT compromise safety. Many transgender people avoid public bathrooms altogether, leading to health problems, missed school, and limited participation in daily life.As Woodhull emphasized in testimony opposing Montana’s HB 121, bathroom bans do NOT make anyone safer; they increase harassment of everyone, force people into unsafe conditions, and violate basic rights to dignity and privacy. These laws and stereotypes isolate transgender people from public life, increase vulnerability to violence, and shift attention away from the real issue: transgender people’s basic right to safety, dignity, and access to public spaces.Are transgender people hypersexual or predatory?NO. Research does NOT suggest that transgender people are hypersexual or more likely to be sexually aggressive.Research shows that transgender folks are NOT more likely than cisgender people to sexually hurt or exploit others. In fact, research shows that transgender people are often the ones getting sexually assaulted. The U.S. Transgender Survey found that 47% of respondents had been sexually assaulted at some point. To put that in perspective, about 19.3% of cisgender women and 1.7% of cisgender men experience sexual violence in their lifetime. Despite being feared as predators, transgender people are far more likely to be victims of abuse and exploitation.The “predatory” framing does more than misrepresent reality: it legitimizes harmful policies and fuels harassment. Incorrect framings of transgender individuals as fundamentally dangerous or abnormal are used to justify increased surveillance of transgender people, keeping them out of certain public areas, and limiting their access to healthcare. For example, Texas Republican Senator Ted Cruz warned that allowing transgender people to use bathrooms matching their gender identity would be “opening the door for predators,” claiming that such laws would let “any man enter a women’s restroom, a little girl’s restroom and stay there.” This rhetoric directly ties trans inclusion to threats against women and children, echoing the same moral panic used against earlier marginalized groups.Rather than protecting communities, this myth perpetuates stigma and violence against transgender people. The stereotype that transgender people are hypersexual or predatory plays on long-standing fears about women’s safety. Throughout history, claims that marginalized groups were sexually dangerous have been used to justify exclusion and violence — first against Black men, then gay men, and now transgender people. Not only does this lead policymakers to overlook the needs of transgender people, but it also overlooks real actual threats to women, children, and other marginalized people.Policy Recommendations1.) Reject bathroom bans.Restricting restroom access harms public health, increases harassment, and violates basic human rights to dignity and privacy. Policies that ensure gender-inclusive restrooms and nondiscrimination protections reduce stigma, improve safety, and affirm the humanity of all people.2.) Affirm access to safe public spaces.Policies that provide gender-inclusive restrooms and nondiscrimination protections, such as ensuring access to single-stall facilities in schools, workplaces, and transportation hubs, reduce harassment and support the health and well-being of all individuals.3.) Protect dignity, privacy, & rights.Bathroom bans undermine the human rights to privacy and personal dignity. By singling out transgender people for surveillance and exclusion, they erode trust in public institutions and create unsafe conditions for everyone. events.text: Warning Non-binary pronouns being taught in Spanish class (FHSD North HS) Non-binary pronouns are absolutely tied to gender identity — that’s not even up for debate. Non-binary pronouns (they/them, ze/zir, xe/xem, etc.) are directly connected to gender identity. Gender identity is how a person understands and experiences their own gender (male, female, both, neither, or somewhere in between). Pronouns are a way language reflects and respects that identity in everyday communication. So when you are teaching students non-binary pronouns, you are, in fact, teaching about gender identity. That is precisely what our policy prohibits. Send concerns to Superintendent mark.delaney@fhsdschools.org and Helene.Herauf@ed.gov to update the open Dept of Education Complaint OCR 07251345

events.text: Probably not too much. But we don’t need authority figures to act like kids. The adults we hire should lead our kids to gain information, wisdom, and good character so that they will be ready to be adults themselves.

events.text: Teacher's use to be professional role models for their students. Not behavior that mimic worse than. Very disturbing to think that is who stands in front of a class to teach and influence successful education.

events.author: Angela Alagna
events.text: Shame on each and every one of you! Our children love their school mostly because of their teachers. This video was created before the school year started while most of these AMAZING people were there prepping for the upcoming school year. And it hyped our kids up. They were excited to go to school and that’s not easy at this age. Find something better to do with your time than complain about some of the hardest working and most caring people in our community. Who are just trying to get everyone ready and excited for the year.

events.author: Joy Hankey

events.author: Joy Hankey
events.text: Jennifer Brinker there is a place and time for "fun". And it should be appropriate for the role you are in in a child's life. Boundaries are needed in certain situations.

events.author: Jennifer Brinker
events.text: I think being fun like this is appropriate for children. I would not find it as appropriate for say… a financial advisor. Fascinating that you see otherwise.

events.author: Nicole Ashraf
events.text: Jane Puszkar that’s an interesting comment. Test scores in my building and grade level have gone up astronomically in the past few years. Also, please remember that kids are far more than a test score. That goes for teachers too. Their ability to teach and reach children can be evaluated by much more than a standardized test score.

events.author: Nicole Ashraf
events.text: Joy Hankey I can assure you that the standard of the test has not been lowered. In fact, in my 14 years of teaching, I have watched state assessments become increasingly rigorous and require students to demonstrate much deeper levels of thinking.And yes, our job is to teach children, but teaching and reaching children are not mutually exclusive. Students cannot effectively learn when they do not feel safe, supported, and connected at school. Maslow’s hierarchy of needs has long demonstrated that basic needs such as safety and belonging must be met before students are able to fully engage in learning.What has changed in recent years is that the district is finally providing teachers with resources that are much more closely aligned with Missouri state standards and evidence-based literacy practices, including the Science of Reading. When teachers have strong, standards-aligned curriculum and students feel safe enough to learn, that is when meaningful academic growth happens.Now that we have a decent reading resource, I’m hopeful that we can get an aligned math resource. We haven’t had math resources aligned with our state standards since 2011 (at least in elementary). Reaching children is part of teaching them.
